papers.title: Artificial intelligence across the continuum of care for the aging musculoskeletal patient: From longitudinal phenotyping to personalized surgery and recovery monitoring
papers.abstract: Abstract Musculoskeletal care is being reshaped by population aging, multimorbidity, frailty, osteoporosis, sarcopenia, polypharmacy and increasing vulnerability to postoperative loss of independence. Artificial intelligence (AI) has entered orthopaedic research, but its clinical translation remains constrained. Many models address isolated diagnostic, imaging or short‐term prediction tasks rather than the longitudinal care trajectories that determine outcomes in older musculoskeletal patients. The central limitation is therefore not simply whether older adults are represented in datasets, but whether AI systems are valid across the continuum of geriatric orthopaedic care. This review argues for a transition from task‐specific orthopaedic AI toward continuum‐of‐care AI for the aging musculoskeletal patient. Upstream, radiomics, longitudinal osteoarthritis phenotyping, opportunistic computed tomography (CT)‐based skeletal assessment and AI‐augmented dual‐energy X‐ray absorptiometry (DXA) modelling may improve prediction of disease progression, fracture risk, treatment failure and surgical timing. At the point of intervention, AI‐assisted arthroplasty planning may help move total knee arthroplasty from generic alignment targets toward phenotype‐specific reconstruction strategies that account for constitutional alignment, bone morphology, ligament envelope, neuromuscular control, frailty and functional reserve. Perioperatively, automated frailty and sarcopenia phenotyping, wearable gait analysis and multimodal temporal models integrating imaging, electronic health records, laboratory data, medications, patient‐reported outcomes and wearable signals may support dynamic risk prediction. After discharge, continuous monitoring of mobility, sleep, pain trajectories, wound‐related symptoms and rehabilitation adherence may help close the high‐risk surveillance gap during the 90‐day postoperative episode. However, clinical adoption requires more than high discrimination. Explainable AI should be understood as one component of a broader trust framework that also includes calibration, uncertainty quantification, decision‐curve analysis, external and prospective validation, workflow integration, post‐deployment monitoring and accountability. The future of orthopaedic AI is not simply better diagnosis or more precise surgery, but longitudinal, multimodal support across the full care continuum: predicting progression, selecting treatment, personalizing surgery, optimizing perioperative care, monitoring recovery and preserving mobility and independence. Level of Evidence Level IV.

papers.title: Textual World Models for Agent Security: Modelling the Internal State of an LLM Agent from Text Alone
papers.abstract: An AI agent chooses its own path to reach an objective, so its security and compliance depend on its internal state, not only on its inputs and outputs. We ask whether the activations of the agent's large language model (LLM), produced when it reads the context, are a sufficient observation of this state to build a model of it, without any access to the agent's tools or design. We test sufficiency by prediction: a world model built on these activations should predict the agent's next step. Because the agent's LLM is usually not accessible, a small witness LLM reads the same context. On 22 agents, the resulting model predicts that the next answer will carry out a prompt-injection attack with an AUROC of 0.93, and identifies the conversation in which the agent will give in for 63 % of pairs that a lookup table cannot separate. The observation is partial, as expected: nothing predicts an attack before it enters the context, because that part of the state is held by the tools.

papers.title: Machine learning–driven strength prediction and optimal waste glass powder dosage for concrete exposed to high temperatures
papers.abstract: This study explores the synergistic effects of the addition of waste glass powder (WGP) and elevated temperatures on the mechanical behavior of concrete, and proposes a machine-learning-based framework for mixture design optimization. Six concrete mixtures containing 0–50% WGP were tested for compressive, flexural, and splitting tensile strengths over the temperature range 24–600 °C, and the results consistently showed an optimal WGP dosage of 10–20% at room temperature and a pronounced degradation in these strengths above 400 °C. To model the strength evolution across the entire WGP-temperature space, a physics-aware data augmentation method and a multi-output Random Forest surrogate model are developed and validated using mixture-wise three-fold cross-validation, parity plots, Y-randomization tests, SHAP-based interpretability analysis, and bootstrap-based uncertainty quantification. The validated surrogate is then combined with NSGA-II to determine WGP dosages that simultaneously maximize room-temperature strength, high-temperature residual capacity, and material efficiency. Both prospective within-domain experimental validation showed close agreement between the surrogate predictions and independently measured responses. Contour maps and optimization results also consistently show that the 10–20% WGP dosage offers the best trade-off between initial strength and thermal resilience. The results demonstrate the two-fold role of WGP as a micro-filler in improving ambient performance and as a thermally sensitive phase governing degradation mechanisms at elevated temperatures. Therefore, this work presents a validated ML-based framework and practical design charts for optimizing WGP-modified concrete for fire-exposed or high-temperature applications. SEM analyses of the glass powder-reinforced concrete sample exposed to 600 °C showed an increase in cracks and voids in the microstructure; EDX results indicated Ca enrichment with the dominance of O (51.49%), Ca (20.78%), and Si (8.17%); FT-IR spectrum showed the disappearance of the ~ 3400 and ~ 1650 cm⁻¹ bands and the weakening of the ~ 950–1000 cm⁻¹ band, confirming C–S–H degradation; and XRD analysis revealed a decrease in amorphous humps and the prominence of crystalline peaks, indicating that the structure became more crystalline and brittle at high temperature. TGA results indicated that room-temperature-cured samples exhibited higher mass loss and progressive degradation at low temperatures, whereas samples pre-exposed to 600 °C exhibited reduced mass loss and enhanced thermal stability, owing to prior dehydration and microstructural reorganization.

papers.title: AI-Driven Early Warning Systems for Flash Floods Using Satellite Imagery: A GeoAI-Based Framework for Real-Time Flash Flood Prediction, Risk Reduction and the Future of Intelligent Disaster Management
papers.abstract: Abstract: Flash floods remain among the most destructive and least predictable hydrometeorological hazards, characterized by rapid onset, localized intense precipitation, and minimal warning time. This paper critically examines whether the convergence of satellite Earth Observation (EO), Artificial Intelligence (AI), and hydrometeorological intelligence can transform flashflood early warning from a predominantly reactive, detectionoriented paradigm into a predictive, anticipatory, and progressively autonomous disaster intelligence system. Through an interdisciplinary synthesis of remote sensing science, deep learning architectures, spatiotemporal modelling, and disaster risk reduction, we propose the AISatellite Flash Flood Early Warning Intelligence Framework (AISFFEWI)—a conceptual architecture that integrates multisource satellite data, groundbased observations, physicsinformed AI, uncertainty quantification, impact forecasting, and community feedback. The study distinguishes carefully between flood detection and actionable early warning, and emphasizes that lead time, false alarm mitigation, and explainability are as critical as prediction accuracy. The paper provides a comprehensive analysis of satellite data sources, AI model suitability, spatiotemporal deep learning, and the severe challenges posed by class imbalance, nonstationary climate conditions, and limited crossregion model transferability. A dedicated Indiacentric perspective examines Himalayan and urban flash floods, while a futureoriented timeline (2026–2050) explores the gradual emergence of AIenabled digital twin watersheds and autonomous warning agents, always balancing technological promise against scientific caution, ethical accountability, and the imperative of communitycentred response. The paper concludes that while satelliteAI systems hold substantial potential to enhance flashflood warning, they cannot replace hydrological understanding, institutional trust, and the human decisionmaking required to convert a probabilistic hazard forecast into lifesaving action.

papers.abstract: The article presents a methodology for refining the thermal model of a public building based on indoor climate monitoring and energy consumption measurements. The relevance of the study stems from the uncertainty of the actual thermal properties of existing buildings and the operating conditions of their heating and ventilation systems, which may lead to substantial discrepancies between calculated and measured energy consumption. The aim is to develop and validate an integrated approach combining on-site measurements, uncertainty quantification, sensitivity analysis, and model calibration. A simplified hourly resistance–capacitance (RC) model using a 3R1C scheme is proposed for simulating the thermal regime of a typical four-storey educational building in Vinnytsia, Ukraine. The uncertainty of nine input parameters is assessed using the Monte Carlo method, while global sensitivity analysis is performed using Sobol indices. The results indicate that the annual space heating demand ranges from 92 to 137 kWh/m² within the 5–95% uncertainty interval. The infiltration air change rate is identified as the dominant parameter, accounting for 64% of the variance in heating demand. Wall thermal transmittance and the indoor temperature setpoint have substantially smaller effects, whereas solar gains and internal heat gains play an important role in determining overheating conditions. The study demonstrates that simultaneous calibration of all influential parameters against heat meter data may produce physically unrealistic parameter estimates due to the compensation of errors. To overcome this limitation, a two-stage calibration procedure is proposed. First, directly measured parameters, including infiltration, ventilation airflow, and indoor temperature, are fixed in the model. The remaining influential parameters are then adjusted through calibration. In a virtual experiment, this approach reduced the monthly normalized mean bias error (NMBE) from 14.5% to 1.0% and reproduced the wall thermal transmittance with an error of 2.6%. The proposed methodology improves the reliability of building energy simulations and provides a basis for substantiated decisions concerning thermal modernization and the optimization of heating and ventilation systems.

papers.title: Adaptive Inversion of the Curie Isothermal Surface in the Ordos Basin and Surrounding Regions Based on Multiple Constraints and Bayesian Optimization
papers.abstract: The Curie isothermal surface (CIS), the depth at which crustal rocks reach the Curie temperature of magnetite, provides important information on the thermal state of the crust and, through it, of the lithosphere. Conventional magnetic anomaly spectral methods for CIS inversion commonly rely on manually selected spectral parameters, leading to considerable subjectivity and uncertainty. This study proposes an adaptive CIS inversion method based on multiple geophysical constraints and Bayesian optimization. The method integrates de-fractal spectral analysis with a Tree-structured Parzen Estimator (TPE) to jointly optimize the fractal index, moving-window size, and spectral fitting ranges for estimating the top and centroid depths of the magnetic layer. Multiple constraints, including heat flow, spatial distribution consistency and effective data coverage, are incorporated into the objective function. Synthetic experiments show that the proposed method improves inversion accuracy, reducing RMSE and MAE by 24.3% and 33.8%, respectively, compared with the conventional fixed-parameter method. Application to the Ordos Basin and surrounding regions reveals CIS depths of 20–40 km, with deeper values in the western and northern parts of the basin interior, and shallower values in the eastern and southern parts of the basin interior and in surrounding tectonic zones. The spatial distribution of the CIS in the study area, together with the crustal structures and the seismicity, helps to clarify the regional thermal state and tectonic evolution.

papers.title: Association of different Factors with Academic Performance Among Optometry Students: A Cross-Sectional Study
papers.abstract: Background: Academic performance among optometry students is influenced by multiple educational, institutional, and personal factors. Understanding these determinants is essential for improving educational quality and producing competent eye-care professionals. Limited evidence is available regarding factors affecting academic achievement among optometry students in India, particularly in Maharashtra. Aim of the study to correlate the different factors with academic performance of optometry students. Methods: A cross-sectional analytical study was conducted among 461 optometry students enrolled in institutions across the Konkan division of Maharashtra. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire assessing academic resources, learning environment, student capacity to engage with learning, and course workload. Academic performance was categorized as unsatisfactory, fair, good, or excellent. Descriptive statistics and Chisquare tests were used to determine associations between educational determinants and academic performance. Results: The mean age of participants was 21.15 ± 1.82 years, and 74.6% were females. Significant associations were observed between academic performance and all educational determinants studied. Academic resources demonstrated a strong association with academic achievement (χ²=256.2, p<0.0001). Students with higher scores in these domains consistently achieved better academic outcomes. Conclusion: Academic performance among optometry students is significantly influenced by academic resources, learning environment, student engagement, and workload management. Student engagement emerged as the most influential determinant. Strengthening educational infrastructure, promoting active learning, and improving academic support systems may enhance academic outcomes and professional competency among optometry students.

papers.title: An Interdisciplinary Framework for Non-Invasive Aesthetic Support in Post-Orthopedic Recovery
papers.abstract: Purpose: This paper examines how non-invasive aesthetic support procedures can be integrated into postoperative orthopedic recovery pathways. Orthopedic interventions frequently entail extended recovery periods marked by discomfort, temporary body image concerns, localized swelling, and reduced physical confidence. Conventional rehabilitation prioritizes mobility restoration and functional recovery, leaving supportive aesthetic approaches underdeveloped within existing recovery frameworks. Methodology: The study developed a patient-centered conceptual model, the Post-Orthopedic Aesthetic Support Framework, through a structured synthesis of the psychosocial, lymphological, and rehabilitation literature. The model was then illustrated by an observational clinical case of a 63-year-old female patient following total hip arthroplasty, assessed over five weeks with Patient-Reported Outcome Measures. Findings: Two modalities, adaptive pressotherapy and microcurrent stimulation, complement established rehabilitation pathways while maintaining a clear distinction between medical treatment and wellness-oriented support. In the observed case, staged aesthetic support was associated with reduced perceived tissue heaviness, faster subjective resolution of visible hematomas, restored sleep quality, and lower reported anxiety. Improved subjective comfort coincided with higher reported adherence to prescribed physical therapy. Unique contribution to theory, practice and policy: The framework converts fragmented evidence on compression therapy and psychosocial support into a single operational pathway with explicit professional boundaries. It supplies aesthetic centers with a safety-bounded referral protocol and provides orthopedic services with a structured option for managing superficial soft-tissue distress after discharge. The model is conceptual and practice-oriented, and it requires further clinical validation.

papers.title: LLM‐Assisted Design of Ultralow‐κ Chalcogenides
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Accelerating the discovery of materials with extreme lattice thermal conductivity () is limited by the high cost of first‐principles screening. Here, we develop an LLM‐assisted low‐ discovery workflow, where Bayesian optimization (BO) proposes candidates, an LLM performs evidence‐conditioned re‐ranking, and physics‐based structure generation, stability validation, and calculations serve as the acceptance criteria. This integration enables efficient candidate prioritization while maintaining rigorous physical validation. The workflow identifies dynamically stable Ag‐based chalcogenides, including Ag 3 SbSe 4 , Ag 4 TiSe 4 , and Ag 4 TiTe 4 . Mechanistic analysis reveals that their ultralow originates from strong phonon renormalization and coherence‐dominated heat transport. Ag 3 SbSe 4 is predicted to reach a maximum of 2.94 at 500 K due to its ultralow of 0.11 W . Furthermore, automated high‐throughput screening of ternary compounds containing 14 elements identifies 2742 dynamically stable materials with W . These results demonstrate that evidence‐conditioned LLM re‐ranking effectively enhances BO‐driven, physics‐validated materials discovery.

papers.title: A Novel Perspective on Explainability: Measuring and Tuning XAI Consensus
papers.abstract: Neural networks are commonly regarded as black boxes, necessitating post-hoc Explainable AI (XAI) methods. However, different feature attribution techniques applied to the same model and data often yield divergent explanations, undermining the reliability of any single method. This work proposes a model-centric approach that moves beyond evaluating individual XAI methods, focusing instead on optimizing neural network architectures toward cross-method consensus via surrogate-based multi-objective hyperparameter tuning. Cross-method XAI consensus, defined as the degree to which diverse attribution techniques yield convergent explanations for a given architecture, is formalized as a novel optimization objective. Consensus is operationalized by aggregating local attributions into global feature importance profiles, standardizing them, and quantifying convergence via the Euclidean distance. This score is integrated as a second objective alongside predictive loss into a Kriging-based Bayesian optimization framework using desirability functions. Empirical evaluation across 14 diverse datasets confirms that explicitly tuning for explainability is feasible. The framework reveals a prevalent performance-explainability trade-off in most in-distribution settings, while analysis of tuning trajectories and selected architectures reveals exploitable structure in the hyperparameter-to-consensus landscape. These findings introduce cross-method XAI consensus as a practical, model-level criterion for neural architecture selection and provide a quantitative basis for analyzing the performance-explainability trade-off.

papers.title: Digital Twins and Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) in Industry 4.0: Real-Time Synchronization, Multi-Scale Simulation, and Edge-Cloud Architectures
papers.abstract: Abstract—The Fourth Industrial Revolution (Industry 4.0) has driven the convergence of physical industrial equipment with high-fidelity virtual models, establishing the paradigm of Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) and Digital Twins (DTs). A production-grade Digital Twin is not merely a static 3D computer-aided design (CAD) asset; it represents an active, bidirectional, and temporally coupled virtual entity that continuously synchronizes with its physical counterpart across the entire operational lifecycle. However, realizing closed-loop autonomous control and multi-scale simulation across distributed smart manufacturing systems presents profound systems engineering challenges: achieving deterministic sub-millisecond synchronization over non-deterministic industrial networks, solving non-linear partial differential equations (PDEs) at edge line rates, harmonizing heterogeneous semantic schemas (e.g., Asset Administration Shells, OPC UA), and maintaining verifiable transactional provenance across multi-tiered supply chains. This paper presents an exhaustive, mathematically formal technical investigation and empirical benchmark of real-time Digital Twins for Industry 4.0. We formalize physical-virtual state divergence under stochastic transport delays, establish the mathematical foundations of Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) as surrogate PDE solvers for real-time finite element analysis (FEA), and model deterministic Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN, IEEE 802.1Qbv) communication bounds. Furthermore, we construct an empirical industrial testbed consisting of an automated robotic manufacturing cell and high-speed CNC milling apparatus connected via a 5G-TSN converged edge-cloud hierarchy. Our empirical results demonstrate that PINN surrogate models reduce thermomechanical stress simulation latency from 4.2 seconds to 8.6 milliseconds (a 488x speedup) while preserving 98.4% structural accuracy compared to classical ANSYS solvers. Concurrently, TSN time-aware traffic scheduling caps physical-to-virtual state synchronization jitter to under 12.4 microseconds. Finally, we establish open research directions in quantum-accelerated multiscale modeling, autonomous twin co-evolution, and zero-trust asset cybersecurity.

papers.title: LINGUACULTURAL REPRESENTATION OF EDUCATION, KNOWLEDGE IN ENGLISH PHRASEOLOGICAL UNITS
papers.abstract: This article examines the linguacultural representation of education and knowledge in English phraseological units. The study is based on the view that phraseological expressions function not only as stable linguistic combinations but also as carriers of culturally significant meanings, values, and ways of conceptualizing human experience. Drawing on approaches to phraseology, сultural studies, and cognitive linguistics, the research explores how education and knowledge are represented through figurative and conventionalized expressions in English. Particular attention is paid to the phraseological units hit the books, learn the ropes, knowledge is power, and know something inside out. The analysis considers their figurative meanings, conceptual structures, and linguacultural significance. The findings demonstrate that education is commonly represented through the concepts of effort, active learning, experience, and practical competence, while knowledge is conceptualized as a source of power, capability, depth, and mastery. The study shows that English phraseological units provide valuable evidence of culturally established attitudes toward learning and intellectual development. Thus, phraseological analysis can contribute to a deeper understanding of the relationship between language, cognition, and culture.

papers.title: THE INTEGRATION OF DIGITAL PEDAGOGY AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN MODERN HIGHER EDUCATION: STRATEGIES, CHALLENGES, AND FUTURE OUTLOOK
papers.abstract: This scientific thesis examines the transformative impact of digital pedagogy and artificial intelligence (AI) integration within modern higher education systems. As educational paradigms shift from traditional instructor-centric models toward personalized, technology-enhanced learning environments, understanding the pedagogical, methodological, and psychological implications becomes critical. The study evaluates adaptive learning platforms, digital assessment tools, and AI-driven instructional scaffolding across diverse academic contexts. Employing a mixed-methods approach comprising empirical classroom surveys, literature synthesis, and qualitative faculty interviews, the research highlights key drivers of student engagement, academic performance retention, and critical thinking development. The findings demonstrate a 28% increase in conceptual retention when digital interactive tools are combined with active learning frameworks. However, significant challenges persist, including digital inequality, algorithmic bias, and the potential degradation of human-to-human pedagogical rapport. The paper concludes with actionable recommendations for curriculum designers, institutional policymakers, and educators aiming to establish an ethically sound, technologically robust educational ecosystem.

papers.title: The new trochanteric nail TFN-A has a higher complication rate in the treatment of proximal femoral fractures than the predecessor model PFN-A
papers.abstract: Abstract Aims Trochanteric fractures (TF) are among the most frequent fractures and have major impact on the affected patients and the healthcare system. Cephalomedullary nails (CMN) are widely used for these fractures. Complications remain frequent, either due to comorbidities or concerning the implant. The goal of this retrospective, single-centre study was to compare the complication rates of two CMN from one manufacturer. Materials and methods All internal fixations TF performed between 01/2017 and 07/2021 in our institution were analysed retrospectively. Follow-up was at least two years. The CMN were the PFN-A or the TFN-A. Demographic data, all reoperations and revisions were recorded. Reoperations and revisions were estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method, with subgrouping as minor reoperation, minor revision or major revision, including conversion to total hip arthroplasty. Results A total of 492 CMN, used in 475 patients, could be included. Among these, 248 were PFN-A and 244 were TFN-A. The overall reoperation rate was 15%, 12.9% for the PFN-A and 17.2% for the TFN-A, respectively. The TFN-A group had significantly more major revisions (hazard ratio 3.57 (95% confidence interval 1.42–9.94; p = 0.004). No relevant differences were found regarding demographic data or the quality of reduction and internal fixation. Discussion The TFN-A had a significantly higher rate of complications leading to major revision than the former PFN-A. This may have been missed when considering only the reoperation rate for all causes due to a camouflage effect by minor complications.

papers.title: An integrated AI-based software architecture for load forecasting, controlled anomaly detection, and predictive energy management
papers.abstract: The increasing deployment of smart meters and Internet of Things technologies has created a demand for intelligent computational systems capable of jointly forecasting electricity consumption, detecting abnormal behavior, and optimizing load management. This study proposes an integrated artificial intelligence-based framework for automated energy metering and consumption management in smart-grid environments. The framework combines a Long Short-Term Memory network for short-term load forecasting, an autoencoder-based model for anomaly detection, and Model Predictive Control for demand-side optimization. The system architecture includes data acquisition, communication, preprocessing, predictive analytics, anomaly monitoring, and decision-support layers. The primary empirical evaluation used 4,380 measured hourly observations (approximately 6 months) from a single administrative building. A separately flagged synthetic temporal extension was retained only as an auxiliary dataset and was excluded from all primary performance metrics. Across five independent model initializations, the final LSTM achieved a MAPE of 3.423 ± 0.555%, an RMSE of 0.336 ± 0.048 kW, and an R 2 of 0.973 ± 0.007 on the 633-sequence independent measured test subset. The synthetic extension was maintained as a separately identified auxiliary component and was excluded from all primary training, validation, and independent test metrics. Using a validation-selected reconstruction-error threshold, the autoencoder detected 12 of 30 controlled anomalies in the independent test subset, yielding 100.00% precision, 40.00% recall, and an F1-score of 57.14%. Under the same controlled protocol, One-Class SVM achieved higher recall (53.33%) and F1-score (69.57%), indicating that the autoencoder should be interpreted as an architectural component rather than as the best-performing anomaly detector for the present dataset. A historical proof-of-concept MPC simulation, retained for architectural illustration, reported a 15% reduction in simulated peak demand and a 12% reduction in estimated electricity cost; these values are not interpreted as measured outcomes from the administrative-building experiment. Controlled anomaly injection was used to establish reproducible validation and test labels for the anomaly-detection component. The results demonstrate that the joint integration of forecasting, anomaly detection, and predictive control provides a computationally coherent framework for supporting energy-management efficiency, operational reliability, and data-driven decision-making in intelligent energy systems.

papers.title: Intelligence-enabled smart inhalable biomaterials for chronic inflammatory airway diseases: integrating responsive carrier engineering, lung-on-chip validation, and patient-specific pulmonary modeling
papers.abstract: Chronic inflammatory airway diseases, particularly asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), are commonly treated by inhalation, yet the nominal dose placed in an inhaler often differs substantially from the dose that reaches diseased airway regions, crosses mucus, enters target cells, and remains pharmacologically active. Airway narrowing, heterogeneous ventilation, mucus plugging, impaired mucociliary clearance, oxidative and proteolytic stress, epithelial barrier dysfunction, inflammatory-cell diversity, device characteristics, and patient-specific inhalation maneuvers jointly shape therapeutic exposure. Smart inhalable biomaterials can be designed to address some of these barriers by controlling transport, retention, activation, or release, but many systems are still optimized primarily at the nanoparticle level and evaluated in static models that do not capture realistic aerosol performance or patient-specific deposition. This review develops an intelligence-enabled bioengineering framework linking disease-informed material design with machine-learning-assisted formulation optimization, formulation–device–patient coupling, lung-on-chip validation, and patient-specific pulmonary modeling. Within this framework, airway features such as mucus architecture, redox gradients, protease activity, epithelial permeability, immune-cell state, extracellular-matrix remodeling, and regional airflow are considered measurable variables that can inform material design and evaluation. The material platforms considered include mucus-penetrating and mucoadhesive carriers, responsive materials, transformable nano-in-micro systems, polymeric and lipid nanoparticles, biomimetic carriers, extracellular vesicles, and systems for pulmonary delivery of nucleic acids and biologics. Their development is considered alongside structured experimental design, machine learning, active learning, mechanistic aerosol modeling, physics-informed surrogates, multi-objective optimization, and uncertainty analysis. Lung-on-chip systems provide human-relevant settings in which deposited dose, mucus transport, barrier function, immune responses, and repeated-exposure effects can be examined under air–liquid-interface and breathing-like conditions. Patient-specific computational fluid dynamics and reduced-order models can complement these platforms by predicting regional deposition, whereas the term digital twin should be reserved for longitudinally updated, uncertainty-aware models linked to actionable decisions. Together, these approaches support a closed-loop design–delivery–validation strategy in which material performance, aerosol behavior, biological response, and patient-specific deposition are evaluated as connected rather than separate development problems.

papers.title: Strip flatness prediction in cold rolling: a review of models, challenges, and emerging directions
papers.abstract: Abstract Cold rolling is one of the most widely applied metal-forming processes, where strip flatness is a critical quality requirement affecting downstream manufacturability, dimensional accuracy and product performance. Flatness defects arise from non-uniform longitudinal stresses generated through tightly coupled interactions between roll bite mechanics, roll stack deformation, friction and lubrication, material behaviour and post-bite buckling. Although numerous modelling strategies exist, the literature remains fragmented across analytical, numerical, hybrid and data driven approaches, making it difficult to identify the most appropriate tools for prediction and control. This review provides a unified framework for strip flatness prediction in cold rolling, presenting a structured taxonomy of modelling approaches and evaluating their assumptions, predictive capability, computational cost and industrial applicability. Analytical and semi-analytical models are compared with numerical techniques and hybrid coupled formulations. Key transversal components, including constitutive laws, friction and lubrication models and buckling formulations, are examined with respect to their influence on widthwise stress distributions and the formation of flatness defects. Recent developments in physics-based, data driven and hybrid modelling, including digital twins and reduced-order models, are discussed with emphasis on their potential to meet the real-time requirements of advanced flatness-control systems. Major research gaps are identified in mixed-lubrication modelling, advanced constitutive descriptions, transient buckling prediction, standardised validation benchmarks and hybrid physics–data driven modelling to support digital twin deployment. By synthesising current knowledge and highlighting emerging research directions, this review provides guidance for selecting and developing strip modelling strategies capable of supporting high precision crown and flatness control in modern, data-enriched rolling mills.

papers.title: A Fusion State-of-Charge Estimation Framework for Lithium-Ion Batteries of Electric Vehicles Using Enhanced Single Particle Model and CNN-BiLSTM
papers.abstract: Abstract Accurate state-of-charge (SOC) estimation is critical for driving range prediction and battery safety in lithium-ion electric vehicles. Purely data-driven methods often lack physical interpretability, whereas electrochemical models are limited by model complexity, parameter identification, and real-time computational burden. This study proposes a physics-guided SOC estimation framework that integrates an enhanced single-particle model (ESPM) with a convolutional bidirectional long short-term memory network (CNN-BiLSTM). The ESPM incorporates electrolyte-phase dynamics and derives electrode utilization variables to describe internal electrochemical states. These physically meaningful variables are combined with measured current, voltage, and temperature as hybrid inputs, while Bayesian optimization is used to tune key hyperparameters. Experiments are performed on A123 lithium iron phosphate cells under FUDS, DST, and US06 profiles from −10 to 40 °C. The proposed framework limits maximum relative SOC errors to 4% under DST and 3% under US06, with maximum RMSE and MAE values of 1.35% and 1.08%. Compared with LSTM, GRU, and CNN-BiLSTM baselines, the framework improves estimation accuracy by 15.16% to 51.06%, demonstrating improved robustness under dynamic and wide-temperature conditions.

papers.title: T2-z: Test-Time Optimization of Environment Latents for Robotic World Models
papers.abstract: Predicting how the world responds to an action requires more than what can be seen: robots must account for environmental factors that are neither directly observable nor explicitly specified, from physical properties such as friction and mass to human-defined environmental rules. We introduce T2-Z for test-time optimization of environment latents, which augments a robotic world model with a learnable environment latent to condition world predictions. This compact latent captures underlying environmental variation without supervision of what environmental factors exist or what values they take. During training, T2-Z alternates between two stages: a world-model optimization stage that fixes the latents and learns general action-conditioned dynamics across environments; and an environment-latent optimization stage that freezes the world model and optimizes the conditioning latents, allowing latent structure to emerge purely through world prediction. At test time, the world model remains frozen and a newly initialized environment latent is optimized from one or more test-time interactions, adapting the model to previously unseen environmental configurations. Across 7 simulated settings and 4 real-world robotic tasks, T2-Z reduces object prediction error metric from 15.20 to 7.00 and raises action success from 33.73% to 72.96%. Its emergent latents capture structured representations of individual and compounded factors across diverse visual scenes. Ablations further show that T2-Z can efficiently infer environment latents from as little as a single test-time interaction trajectory.

papers.title: GeoState: Learning View-Decoupled Geometry States for 3D World Modeling
papers.abstract: Recent 3D world models increasingly use features from geometry foundation models (GFMs) as predictive world states, benefiting from their rich geometric priors. However, the view dependence of these features entangles scene dynamics with camera-induced variation, making the resulting state evolution harder to predict. We propose GeoState, a view-decoupled geometry representation for predictive 3D world modeling that separates scene-state evolution from camera-dependent observation. Specifically, a scene tokenizer aggregates multi-view GFM features into a view-decoupled scene state, which a geometry decoder queries using camera rays. An autoregressive world model then predicts future scene states, while camera motion is modeled separately. The predicted states can therefore be decoded under either predicted or externally specified cameras, while retaining a single context-derived scale throughout the rollout without per-frame scale alignment. Experiments show that GeoState outperforms prior 3D world models on Waymo, supports geometrically consistent cross-view querying, and generalizes zero-shot to KITTI and nuScenes. Project page: https://hongchang-liu.github.io/GeoState-project-page/

papers.title: Dexterity from Supervised Play
papers.abstract: How can robots autonomously collect the contact-rich experience needed to learn dexterous manipulation? We present DSP: Dexterity from supervised play, a framework in which a robot learns a play policy from minutes of human play through behavior cloning, then deploys it autonomously to collect hours of interaction data to train a world model. During inference, the same play policy then guides model-predictive control (MPC) by proposing candidate action sequences for evaluation under the learned world model. To accelerate inference, we also introduce a method for distilling a closed-loop, goal-conditioned policy through self-play within the learned world model. We evaluate this framework on underactuated pushing and any-to-any in-hand pose reorientation with a multifingered hand, in simulation and real world. In real world experiment, our method outperforms hindsight behavior cloning by 69.6% in success rate and achieves comparable success to reinforcement learning with 490 times less interaction data. These results demonstrate that supervised play can autonomously collect interaction data, guide model-based planning, and enable policy learning without any task-specific demonstrations or sim-to-real transfer.

papers.title: Sim-to-Real Reinforcement Learning for Path-Safe Target Reaching in Robotic Harvesting of Hydroponic Lettuce
papers.abstract: Robotic harvesting requires precise manipulation to ensure accurate positioning of the end-effector, especially in a constraint workspace. This study introduces the Path-Safe Approach Proximal Policy Optimization (PSA-PPO), a target-conditioned local reaching framework designed for robotic harvesting of nutrient film technique (NFT)-hydroponic lettuce in greenhouses. The proposed PSA-PPO preserves the standard clipped PPO objective while introducing a harvesting-oriented policy formulation that integrates target-conditioned observations, corridor-aware spatial constraints, trajectory-history-based safety encoding, and task-specific success criteria for constrained robotic manipulation. PSAPPO was trained entirely in Isaac Lab and successfully transferred to a physical UR10e robotic arm without any real-world policy fine-tuning. In a controlled physical benchmark against 150 scheduled targets, PSA-PPO achieved the highest reaching rate of 94.7%, outperforming Cartesian+TOTG (86.0%), RRTConnect (88.0%), and RRT* (80.0%), while reducing median RMS jerk by 39.8 to 73.0% relative to the classical planners during the final approach segment. A formulation ablation evaluated over 200 simulation targets demonstrates that path-safety and side-corridor shaping are the principal drivers of harvesting-compatible performance: removing either term substantially degrades strict success even when terminal endpoint accuracy is preserved or improved, confirming that optimization toward the endpoint alone is an insufficient objective for constrained crop-proximal manipulation. Finally, PSA-PPO was integrated with an RGB-D vision module and an end-effector and evaluated as a complete greenhouse harvesting system across 144 lettuce harvesting attempts, achieving 94.4% vision-guided target reaching and 86.1% complete harvesting success.

papers.title: X-RIC: An Agentic RAN-Intelligent Controller Benchmark for Enhancing Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: The O-RAN ALLIANCE introduces architectural flexibility through disaggregation and AI-driven control. While the RAN Intelligent Controller (RIC) enables centralized optimization, current AI approaches lack reasoning capabilities and explainability. We propose eXplainable RIC (X-RIC), a novel framework integrating agentic AI into O-RAN architectures. X-RIC combines reactive Reinforcement Learning (RL) with strategic agentic reasoning through: (i) automated Behavioral Cloning (BC) using domain heuristics for sample-efficient training, (ii) a Telecom Language Model (TLM), a transformer-based reasoning module providing contextual abstraction and interpretability, and (iii) closed-loop co-adaptation within the Near-RT RIC control loop enabling continuous policy refinement. To ensure deployment readiness, we introduce BARX (Benchmarking Agentic Reasoning for RAN), a domain-specific evaluation framework assessing agentic control across latency, compliance, and determinism metrics. We validate X-RIC on SLA-aware network slicing in simulation and O-RAN-compliant testbed deployments. X-RIC achieves 89% operational cost reduction while maintaining SLA compliance, converging 75% faster with 50% fewer training steps and 46% lower variance.

papers.title: Safe and Fuel-Efficient Motion Planning for Lunar Propulsive Drones
papers.abstract: Propulsive drones are a promising new technology for generating high-resolution terrain models of the Moon. In future lunar missions, propulsive drones will complete a series of hops across the lunar surface while capturing images with downward-facing cameras. We present an autonomous motion planning framework that uses a vision-guided optimal control strategy for performing safe, efficient hops between specified waypoints. The drone plans parabolic hops between waypoints generated by a global-level planner; if a nominal waypoint is unsafe or unreachable, the drone then completes a diversion maneuver to safely land. To evaluate the validity of potential landing sites, we develop a custom semantic segmentation model for identifying obstacles from aerial images, and we introduce an approach for rapidly calculating reachable terrain. We then use model predictive control (MPC) to robustly track hop trajectories that guide the drone towards safe landing sites. We test the optimal hop planner in a high-fidelity lunar simulation environment. Our results demonstrate that our unified motion planning framework yields safe, fuel-efficient hop trajectories which can be tracked rapidly and with low error via MPC.

papers.title: Inertially Significant Humanoid Teleoperation via Whole Body Model Predictive Control and Online Parameter Estimation
papers.abstract: The effective deployment of humanoid robots in practical tasks of interest will require a capability of sensing and adapting to variations in inertial parameters, as occurs during heavy tool use or when carrying significant payload. Such payloads constitute a significant proportion of the combined payload-robot system, the effects of which cannot be ignored by delegating to feedback control. This paper showcases a general solution to this problem by integrating a whole body model predictive controller (WB-MPC) with an extended Kalman filter (EKF) for online estimation of fully physically consistent time-varying inertial parameters. These estimates are fed through to the WB-MPC's full rigid body dynamics model, resulting in more accurate feedforward torques for task demands under external load. Additionally, a virtual reality (VR) interface is provided that enables an operator to provide task-specific references without regard to payload while delegating dynamic balance to the WB-MPC. The framework is validated with simulation and hardware experiments on a humanoid system.

papers.title: The importance of tensor handling and implementation of physics-informed DeepONets
papers.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) reduce or eliminate the need for large labelled datasets by enforcing governing equations during training. Physics-informed Deep Operator Networks (PI-DeepONets) extend this approach to learning solution operators, enabling rapid prediction across families of problems. Despite these advantages, we show that their application to higher-dimensional problems remains limited by the computational cost of training. To address this issue, we propose a modified PI-DeepONet architecture that reduces this cost by removing redundancy in how the Branch network processes input functions across collocation points. The proposed formulation is mathematically equivalent to the original architecture but reduces input tensor sizes and the number of Branch network evaluations. We analyse the computational complexity of both architectures and derive theoretical scaling laws for training time with respect to the number of collocation points and input functions. The proposed architecture is evaluated on 1D, 2D, and 3D linear advection problems. In all cases, it achieves comparable predictive accuracy to the original PI-DeepONet while consistently reducing training time. In 2D experiments, a maximum speed-up of $3.75\times$ is observed, with empirical training-time scaling agreeing with the predicted linear dependence on collocation points and input functions. Furthermore, training a 3D model on an NVIDIA A100 GPU is only feasible using the proposed architecture, as the original formulation exceeds memory limits. These results demonstrate that careful consideration of how PI-DeepONets are implemented can yield substantial gains, enhancing the practical performance of PI-DeepONets and enabling their application to otherwise intractable physics-informed learning problems.

papers.title: Beyond Fixed Acquisition Functions: Temporal Difference Active Learning for Perturbation Discovery
papers.abstract: Genetic and drug perturbation screens are important tools for elucidating disease mechanisms and validating therapeutic targets, but experimental costs limit the number of candidates that can be tested. Existing perturbation screening methods typically update the surrogate model with feedback while keeping the acquisition function fixed, limiting their ability to adapt selection to different response landscapes. Experimental feedback reveals current hits and informs subsequent selection by updating candidate predictions, providing a training signal for learning how to select experiments. We formulate budgeted perturbation discovery as a sequential decision problem and propose Temporal Difference Active Learning (TDAL), which learns an acquisition function online through temporal difference learning from a single screening trajectory, accounting for current hits and future discoveries. TDAL uses the Hellinger distance between hit probabilities for unmeasured candidates before and after an experiment to weight successor value, and reuses measured outcomes through leave-batch-out (LBO) to construct virtual transitions and alleviate training data scarcity. Across eight public screens spanning single, double, and triple perturbations under varied experimental configurations, TDAL achieves an average rank of 1.63 among eleven methods and ranks first on four tasks, demonstrating its adaptability across response landscapes.

papers.title: The Snapping Phenomenon and Boundary Enforcement in Model Reduction: Mechanisms and Mitigation
papers.abstract: Projection-based model order reduction mitigates the computational cost of high-fidelity parametric simulations but can suffer from the "snapping phenomenon", whereby a projection-based reduced-order model (PROM) rigidly latches onto a training snapshot, impairing parametric interpolation. Standard methods also struggle to enforce parameter-dependent boundary conditions without costly constraints or penalty schemes. This work proposes a tripartite taxonomy of snapping, distinguishing intrinsic, extrinsic, and numerical mechanisms. Focusing on intrinsic and numerical snapping, we introduce a unified framework based on a parameter-dependent shift vector. By embedding spatial transport into the state ansatz, the method enforces boundary conditions exactly, restores continuous parametric sensitivity, and eliminates snapshot latching in affine and regression-augmented PROMs without increasing online complexity. We establish the framework's mathematical foundations in the linear regime, showing how it overcomes test-space orthogonality blind spots. In nonlinear computational fluid dynamics, we identify the roles of boundary conditions, mesh grading, and discrete equation scaling in numerical snapping. We also show that formulation-toggling is an unreliable heuristic that can compromise near-field accuracy. Finally, we develop a field-theoretic realization using a spatially varying shift vector governed by a scaled Laplace equation. The approach is validated on structural and aerodynamic benchmarks, including viscous flow around a NACA airfoil and a three-dimensional NASA Common Research Model.

papers.title: Plans Are Not Executions: Adapting Frozen World-Model Planners to Controller-Induced Execution Shift
papers.abstract: World-model planners evaluate candidate trajectories by predicting their future consequences, implicitly relying on the plan-to-motion relationship learned during training. At deployment, a different downstream controller may execute the same planned trajectory differently, creating a planning-execution gap between the frozen model's imagined future and actual execution. A natural remedy is to replace the planned trajectory with its predicted or observed execution. However, we find that better execution fidelity does not necessarily yield better decisions: directly substituting predicted execution trajectories yields only a 0.048 PDMS improvement across 10 unseen controller configurations, far smaller than the gain from our proposed adaptation. This suggests a semantic mismatch between a planned trajectory, which serves as a reference for downstream control, and an executed trajectory, which already describes the resulting post-controller motion.   We introduce ExecutionBridge, which infers controller-specific execution characteristics from planned-executed trajectory pairs and uses them to adapt the native ego latent rollout while keeping the original planned trajectory unchanged. The planner, world model, and reward head remain frozen. On NAVSIM, ExecutionBridge consistently improves planning across unseen controller configurations and multiple frozen world-model planners, with substantially larger gains in challenging driving scenes where execution mismatch more strongly affects candidate evaluation.

papers.title: GraphACM: Graph-based Action Consistency Measurement for Uncertainty Quantification in LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Behavioral consistency across repeated executions provides an informative signal for assessing the reliability of large language model (LLM) agents. However, existing approaches typically summarize consistency with a single task-level score, without identifying where behavioral differences occur or whether actions are compared under equivalent decision contexts. We propose a graph-based framework for fine-grained behavioral consistency measurement and uncertainty quantification. Given multiple rollouts of the same task, we merge equivalent states into a directed, action-labeled graph, enabling action comparisons at shared decision states. We introduce node-level and global measures of action consistency, using the global consistency score as a proxy for uncertainty to predict task success or failure. Experiments across three LLMs on ALFWorld, AppWorld, and WebShop demonstrate that our measure is positively associated with task success and achieves an average AUROC of 0.811 for task-success prediction, outperforming the strongest behavioral-consistency baseline (0.729) and verbalized confidence (0.769). These results highlight the effectiveness of state-conditioned behavioral consistency and pinpoint where agent actions agree.

papers.title: VeriVLA: Adaptive Test-Time Verification for Flow-Based VLAs with Latent World Models
papers.abstract: Flow-based Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies are inherently stochastic: different noise seeds can produce action chunks of varying quality from the same observation. At test time, however, the policy typically commits to a single sample without an explicit estimate of its quality. In fine-grained manipulation, executing a suboptimal action can irreversibly disrupt task progress and lead to failure. To exploit policy stochasticity, we introduce a training-free two-axis trigger that uses two initial samples to measure within-chunk temporal variation and cross-sample variance, detecting the critical states. Once triggered, a JEPA-based latent world model ranks candidate action chunks by predicting action-conditioned future latent states and the corresponding changes in task progress. By operating in latent space, the verifier avoids pixel reconstruction and enables efficient and more accurate ranking. Across three real-world tasks, $\textit{i.e.,}$ pen insertion, pipetting, and apple placement), our method raises the average completion score from 50.8% to 65.5%, while adding 326 ms for sampling and verification per triggered decision on a single RTX 4090. Consistent gains are also observed in simulation, where the average success rate rises from 66.4% to 73.6% in the clean setting of RoboTwin 2.0, from 62.8% to 69.6% in its randomized setting, and from 96.9% to 97.6% on LIBERO.

papers.title: Learn Only Where You Can't Compute: Structured Corrections to Gaussian Process Posteriors
papers.abstract: Physics-informed Gaussian processes (GPs) provide a principled framework for scientific inference by expressing uncertainty over empirical measurements, boundary conditions, and governing equations. However, they struggle to scale to larger datasets and nonlinear information. Conversely, diffusion models excel at learning complex distributions over functions from massive datasets, but struggle in scientific contexts where training data are scarce and physical or observational information must be incorporated. We propose a structured posterior-correction framework that combines a tractable Gaussian reference with data-driven corrections via generative learning. After a mean correction and covariance calibration, a diffusion model learns a targeted correction in a low-dimensional subspace selected to capture discrepancies from the reference, while the complement retains its Gaussian law. Across three scientific inference tasks, these corrections recover hidden modes, improve sample structure, and reduce prediction error relative to the Gaussian reference. Comparisons with full-field generative models reveal task-dependent benefits and tradeoffs between predictive accuracy and computational cost.

papers.title: De-Risking Robotic Welding for In-Space Metal Joining Through Physics-Grounded Digital Twins
papers.abstract: Growing interest in in-space servicing, manufacturing, and assembly has renewed attention on reliable metal joining for modular construction and on-orbit repair. Robotic welding is promising, but reduced-gravity and low-pressure operation remains poorly characterised and flight-like tests are limited. The UK Space Agency-supported ISPARK project is developing a physics-grounded digital twin for structured process de-risking. This paper evaluates a model-based prototype combining a finite-volume thermal weld-pool model, Gaussian-process (GP) and neural-network surrogates, and a simulated six-axis manipulator. The reduced model includes solid-liquid phase change, effective thermocapillary transport, and a local-pressure parameter. Gravity is assessed separately through a hydrostatic-to-capillary pressure ratio and does not enter the thermal energy equation. Across repeated five-fold cross-validation, the GP has lower normalised mean absolute error than the neural network for all eight outputs. In 10 held-out boundary cases, 74 of 80 solver responses fall within nominal 90% GP predictive intervals. A three-output GP query takes 249 microseconds, including scaling and predictive variance. In a simulated UR5 L-shaped-seam study, a proportional controller adjusts the synergic power-source setting as travel speed falls near the corner. Finite-volume re-evaluation finds all 12 closed-loop operating points and 9 of 12 open-loop points within an illustrative 1.0-3.0 mm root-side-width band. These simulation results support using the framework to screen welding conditions and control strategies before experimental tests. Thermal-vacuum, targeted reduced-gravity, and robotic hardware-in-the-loop studies are needed to assess the model and controller.

papers.title: CoWorld Reasoner: Agentic Multimodal Reasoning with the Evolving Video World Model-Driven Harness
papers.abstract: As Vision-Language Models (VLMs) advance, they are increasingly expected to perform spatiotemporal reasoning over motion, actions, and view changes beyond what the input images show. Video World Models (VWMs) provide a natural unified engine for visual imagination by generating task-relevant visual content as additional evidence. However, existing approaches typically invoke a VWM through fixed pipelines centered on a predefined form of visual imagination, such as novel-view synthesis. To support flexible visual imagination for diverse reasoning tasks, we introduce CoWorld Reasoner, an agentic framework that uses a VWM as a unified visual reasoning engine. Its Video World Model-Driven Harness exposes multiple visual operations through tools and uses skills to guide the VLM in deciding whether to imagine, selecting an operation, constructing a generation request, and interpreting the resulting visual evidence. We further introduce VLM-VWM Harness Co-Evolution, which jointly revises tools, skills, and execution code based on execution feedback while keeping both model weights fixed. Across seven benchmarks spanning spatial intelligence, temporal and causal reasoning, and perceptual reasoning, CoWorld Reasoner outperforms direct reasoning with the same VLM. The strongest variant improves on all seven benchmarks, including relative accuracy gains of 11.8% on MMSI and 13.0% on ERQA, and outperforms all five evolving baselines using the same backbone across five benchmarks.

papers.title: MAIA: Anticipating Interaction Anomalies in Contact-Rich Manipulation via Multimodal World Models
papers.abstract: Reliable contact-rich manipulation requires detecting execution deviations early enough for corrective action. Yet most monitoring methods are reactive, identifying anomalies only after they become observable. Anticipating such anomalies is challenging because visual observations only partially reveal physical interaction, while planned actions describe intended motion rather than their actual physical consequences. We address this problem with MAIA, a multimodal framework for anomaly anticipation. Its vision-action-force world model learns nominal interaction dynamics and predicts the visual and force responses of planned actions, while a lightweight anomaly head predicts impending interaction anomalies. To enable systematic evaluation, we introduce CRIA, a real-world multimodal dataset of 2,852 trajectories spanning 18 contact-rich manipulation tasks, with frame-level annotations of anomaly onset and evolution. Experiments on both seen and novel tasks show that MAIA achieves more accurate anomaly discrimination than representative baselines while providing earlier warnings, with bACC scores of 0.765 and 0.710 and median anticipation lead times of 28.0 and 25.1 steps, respectively. Moreover, using these predictions for anomaly-aware action selection improves end-to-end task success from 52.6% to 61.5% without retraining the underlying manipulation policy. These results highlight the value of modeling future physical consequences for proactive anomaly anticipation.

papers.title: A Decision-Aware Evaluation Protocol for Uncertainty in Medical Image Segmentation
papers.abstract: Medical segmentation uncertainty is often evaluated with calibration error or pixel-level error-detection scores, but these metrics do not show whether uncertainty improves downstream review decisions. We propose a decision-aware evaluation protocol that separates uncertainty estimation from deferral policy and evaluates their combination under fixed review budgets: which pixels, regions, or images should be accepted, and which should be reviewed. The protocol reports fixed-budget error reduction, risk-coverage behaviour, region-level review proxies, structural failure modes, probability-derived baselines, and sensitivity to review assumptions. We instantiate it across retinal vessel, skin lesion, and polyp segmentation with multiple backbones and uncertainty estimators. Under matched inference budgets and canonical multi-layer MC Dropout, test-time augmentation (TTA) gives a stronger error-detection signal across matched MC--TTA comparisons, including architecture and dropout-placement checks. However, estimator rankings are not universal. For example, probability-derived scores remain competitive, deep ensembles can outperform TTA, learned deferral helps mainly when the base estimator is weak, and rankings can change with review unit, uncertainty target, correction assumptions, and cost model. Structural and second-observer analyses further show that boundary and thin-structure failures are partly tied to annotation ambiguity. These findings support evaluating uncertainty as an estimator-policy-review configuration, not as a standalone score map. Code: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/Uncertainity-in-Medical-Image-Segmentation/README.md

papers.title: Uncertainty Quantification in Pairwise Difference Learning for Classification
papers.abstract: Instead of learning a mapping from instances to outcomes in the standard way, the key idea of pairwise difference learning (PDL) is to learn a function that takes two instances as input and predicts the difference between the respective outcomes. Given a function of this kind, predictions for a query instance are derived from every training example and then averaged. We propose a version of PDL for the task of classification and propose a suitable meta-learning technique for this purpose. Moreover, we address the problem of uncertainty quantification, i.e., of representing and quantifying the uncertainty of a PDL classifier's predictions in a faithful manner. Building on recent work on the decomposition of total uncertainty into aleatoric and epistemic components, we propose different ways of extending corresponding measures to the setting of PDL, depending on how and to what extent uncertainty is represented by the underlying base learner. In large-scale empirical studies, we analyze both the predictive accuracy and the uncertainty awareness of our PDL classifier.

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning-driven Diffusion Models: Language, Vision, and Beyond
papers.abstract: Diffusion models (DMs) have steadily demonstrated outstanding performance in high-fidelity, controllable generation across diverse scenarios, following the "pretraining-finetuning" paradigm established in LLMs. Despite these advances, conventional DMs still face critical limitations in sophisticated reasoning, autonomous exploration of generation pathways, and adaptability to complex, human-aligned objectives. Inspired by RLHF's success in LLMs, RL has recently emerged as a pivotal post-training mechanism to iteratively refine DMs through reward-driven trajectory optimization. This paper presents the first comprehensive review of RL-driven DMs and an empirical analysis of how RL reshapes the diffusion process towards experience-centric, goal-directed generation. We propose a novel technical panorama elucidating RL's multifaceted roles in diffusion-based language, multimodal, robotic, and scientific models, with a granular focus on diffusion trajectory optimization and reward engineering. Through extensive experiments on multiple task-specific benchmarks, we systematically evaluate representative methods to intuitively highlight the advantages of different RL post-training strategies. Furthermore, we reveal and dissect three crucial bottlenecks that currently hinder the real-world deployment of RL-driven DMs: reward design fragility, exploration-exploitation trade-off in high-dimensional generation spaces, and training instability under sparse rewards. Based on these perspectives, we provide a principled roadmap for the integration of RL into DMs and outline promising future research directions for robust, interpretable RL-diffusion systems. We also construct a public repository to continuously track the latest developments in this rapidly evolving field: https://github.com/MAIR-Lab-HUST/Awesome-RL-for-Diffusion-Models.

papers.title: From Optical Flow to Safety: Visual Safety Certification via Scale-Free Relative Motion
papers.abstract: Safe autonomous navigation using monocular vision remains challenging because explicit obstacle states are not directly observable. This letter introduces a visual safety-certification paradigm that uses scale-free, depth-normalized relative motion encoded by monocular optical flow as the representation for collision-risk certification, without reconstructing obstacle position, velocity, geometry, or a metric world model. Unlike conventional optical-flow-based navigation approaches that rely on image motion to shape avoidance behavior, the proposed framework directly encodes collision-cone geometry and safety constraints in this relative-motion representation. An online Concurrent Learning observer estimates the normalized relative velocity and provides a computable estimation-error bound. This uncertainty is propagated into the collision cone through angular inflation and a monocular robot-footprint margin, yielding a Robust Vision-Based Collision Cone Control Barrier Function (RV-C$^3$BF). An optimal-decay CBF quadratic program minimally modifies the nominal control input to enforce the resulting robust safety constraint under the stated assumptions. Extensive simulation and real-world experiments on a TurtleBot3 in cluttered environments with static and dynamic obstacles demonstrate collision avoidance using only monocular vision and onboard proprioception, with the estimation-error bound containing the measured error in $98.3\%$ of simulation samples and the robot achieving collision-free navigation in $93$ of $100$ real-world trials.

papers.title: Same Target, Different Origins: Aligning Latent Rollout for Consistent PDE Emulation
papers.abstract: Neural PDE solvers commonly generate multi-step predictions through autoregressive rollout, recursively applying a learned evolution operator and feeding each prediction back as input for the next step. Approximation errors can therefore propagate through the rollout, causing predictions at a shared target time to depend on their temporal origins and rollout depths. For a well-posed deterministic PDE flow, however, states at different times along the same physical trajectory should, under exact evolution, reach the same target state. To this end, we propose Align Latent Rollout (ALR), a regularization approach that promotes consistency across rollout origins through the neural PDE solver's internal representations. A second-order Taylor analysis of latent discrepancy propagation motivates two objectives: zeroth-order latent state consistency, which aligns representations at a shared target time, and first-order latent dynamics consistency, which aligns local evolution responses to shared perturbations. ALR can be integrated into different neural PDE solvers by regularizing suitable internal representations, without modifying their backbone architectures. Experiments across multiple PDE benchmarks and neural-operator backbones show that ALR improves prediction accuracy while reducing shared-target discrepancies across rollout origins.

papers.title: CQDC-Warp: GPU-Accelerated Differentiable Quasi-Dynamic Simulation for Contact-Rich Manipulation
papers.abstract: Efficient synthesis of contact-rich manipulation trajectories is essential for downstream robot learning. Gradient-based planning offers a promising approach, but jointly optimizing motion and contact decisions remains challenging. Meanwhile, many existing planners run on CPUs with limited throughput. We present CQDC-Warp, a GPU-accelerated differentiable quasi-dynamic simulator for batched model predictive control (MPC). We use it to study contact-guided trajectory optimization, in which intended robot--object contacts are specified before planning and encouraged through soft costs, while the simulated dynamics determine contact geometry and frictional response without a prescribed contact-mode schedule. Across $17{,}408$ trials on the $17$-object Allegro in-hand rotation benchmark, our framework achieves $79.8\%$ success, compared with $73.7\%$ for CFree and $65.2\%$ for IMPACT, and reduces mean trajectory-generation time by factors of $27.0$ and $50.2$, respectively. On a single NVIDIA RTX 4090 with $2{,}048$ parallel worlds, forward and backward throughput reach $2.06\times10^5$ and $2.25\times10^5$ world-steps per second, respectively. Further experiments cover manipulation with LEAP and Shadow hands, environmental contact exploitation, bimanual manipulation, whole-body control, and real-world trajectory replay on a Sharpa hand.

papers.title: MR-MPCC: Model Predictive Contouring Control for Robotic Manipulator Tracking under Moving Reference Frames
papers.abstract: Maintaining small path-tracking errors under moving reference frames is essential for robotic manipulation tasks with tight execution tolerances, such as machining and surgical automation. Conventional time-indexed controllers, including tracking Model Predictive Control (MPC), rely on a fixed temporal correspondence with the reference trajectory and may therefore accumulate path-relative error under abrupt reference-frame motion or timing mismatch. This paper presents MR-MPCC, a Model Predictive Contouring Control (MPCC) framework for velocity-controlled robotic manipulators with 6-DoF end-effector pose regulation under Moving-Reference disturbances. A hierarchical control architecture is adopted, in which an upper-level MPCC optimizes path progress while penalizing contouring and orientation errors, and a constrained resolved motion rate control (RMRC) layer maps the commanded Cartesian twist to feasible joint velocities under joint-level and safety constraints. MR-MPCC is implemented in a ROS2--MuJoCo pipeline and validated on a UR5e platform under moving-reference disturbances, where the path frame is perturbed and tracked by electromagnetic sensors. Compared with PI control and time-indexed tracking MPC under matched disturbance, MR-MPCC achieves lower geometric path-following error and smaller deviations in the moving path frame, demonstrating improved path-following performance under reference-frame motion.

papers.title: Manifold Generative Annealing for Contact Constraint-aware Impedance Control with Reinforcement Learning Prior
papers.abstract: Contact-rich robotic tasks require coordinated motion and impedance under uncertain interaction dynamics and physical constraints. While recent methods on learned policies provide useful interaction strategies, they may fail when contact conditions differ from those encountered during training. Model-based generative methods show promising receding-horizon trajectories optimization results, but often lack structured behavioral guidance and refinement that jointly accounts for constraint geometry and actual contact responses. To this end, we propose Manifold Generative Annealing (MGA), a joint model-free and model-based generative framework for motion--impedance optimization. MGA first organizes pretrained reinforcement learning policies into structured sequence proposals, retaining task-specific interaction strategies without committing to their execution. It then evaluates these proposals alongside exploratory samples through model-based rollouts for refinement or separate execution selection. Crucially, realization-aware manifold refinement aligns updates from the refinement bank with both task constraints and locally achievable physical responses, allowing learned experience to guide online adaptation under changing contact conditions. Experiments cover surface scanning, peg insertion, and humanoid pushing, with improved safety success rate of impedance control under nominal and sensing-shift conditions.

papers.title: Stochastic Latent Twins: Learning Stochastic Solution Operators
papers.abstract: Scientific prediction under uncertainty requires more than a single future state: it requires the distribution of possible outcomes. We show that this distribution-valued evolution can be learned directly as a stochastic solution operator between arbitrary source and target times. We introduce Stochastic Latent Twins, which represent the physical state through a deterministic encoder-decoder while placing stochasticity entirely in a probability-valued latent evolution map. This separation makes the stochastic transition law independent of the state representation and enables direct probabilistic prediction without recursive time stepping.   We establish an end-to-end Wasserstein approximation theory that separates representation and latent-transition errors, derive stability guarantees, and develop a distributional theory of physics conformity with latent-to-physical transfer bounds and conformity by construction. The resulting framework can be learned directly from observed transitions and supports forward prediction, backward conditional evolution, one-shot generation, and physics-conforming stochastic dynamics within the same formulation. Numerical experiments ranging from linear and non-Gaussian SDEs to stochastic Lorenz dynamics, generative modeling, a stochastic Hamiltonian system, and a two-dimensional stochastic Burgers equation verify the theory, expose the distinct roles of state representation and transition-family expressivity, compare favorably with recent stochastic and one-step generative methods, and demonstrate exact physical conservation by construction. More broadly, Stochastic Latent Twins provide a step toward scientific surrogates that represent not only the evolution of a system, but also its uncertainty and physical structure, opening new opportunities across uncertainty quantification, data assimilation, inverse problems, control, and digital twins.

papers.title: Immediate Implant Placement With Peri-Implant Contour Augmentation in the Maxillary Central Incisor: A Three-Year Clinical and Cone-Beam Computed Tomography Follow-Up
papers.abstract: Although immediate implant placement in the anterior maxilla can shorten the treatment timeline, it presents challenges in preserving peri-implant hard-and soft-tissue contours.We report the three-year clinical and radiographic outcome of immediate implant placement combined with peri-implant contour augmentation in the region of the maxillary right central incisor.A 20-year-old man presented two months after trauma with a non-restorable cervical fracture of the maxillary right central incisor.Clinical and conebeam computed tomography (CBCT) evaluation demonstrated facial bone deficiency with sufficient apical and palatal bone for immediate implant placement.Following atraumatic extraction, a 4 × 14 mm implant was placed in a prosthetically driven three-dimensional position with primary stability of 35 Ncm.The periimplant gap and facial contour were augmented using deproteinized bovine bone mineral (Bio-Oss®, Geistlich Pharma AG, Wolhusen, Switzerland) and a resorbable collagen membrane.Following uneventful healing, second-stage surgery was performed at three months, followed by definitive ceramic crown placement.At the three-year follow-up, the implant remained clinically stable, with healthy peri-implant soft tissues and preserved facial contour, without signs of inflammation, infection, or mobility.CBCT demonstrated maintained bone in the crestal and mid-buccal regions, with satisfactory osseointegration and preservation of peri-implant hard-tissue support.Careful case selection, atraumatic extraction, prosthetically driven implant positioning, primary stability, and appropriate management of facial bone deficiencies are important considerations for achieving predictable outcomes.
