papers.title: 3D Printing of PA12 / CF Composite to Fabricate Equation‐Driven Möbius Strip Lattice for Small‐Scale Drone Frame
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Small‐scale drones have a bright future in agriculture. These kinds of drones require longer operational time, which is possible with reduced power consumption. The drone's weight is critical for longer operations. The lattice structure is well known for its lightweight and better strength‐to‐weight ratio. These lattices could be used to fabricate the drone frame, potentially providing lightness, a better strength‐to‐weight ratio, and reduced power consumption. The Möbius strip has a natural twist that could help distribute the load. PA12/CF lattice with predetermined stress‐concentration points (twist), fabricated from a PA12/CF for drone bodies, is very limited in the literature. First, static loading was applied, and stress–strain behavior was observed across three distinct zones, with a total energy absorption of 129 kJ/m 3 . Strengthening behavior after the elastic limit and considerable toughness before fracture was observed. Dynamic compression proved the 89% recovery after cyclic loading. FEM results showed that bending is the dominant failure mode, with the twist section as the primary failure location. Matrix yield at the material level played a major role in failure. An artificial neural network (ANN) used for surrogate model training and Pareto‐front multi‐objective optimization yielded the maximum‐modulus shape of Möbius strip lattice used in the drone frame.

papers.title: Variational quantum principal component analysis for Hilbert space Gaussian process regression
papers.abstract: Abstract Gaussian processes are widely used probabilistic models for regression and classification tasks. Their flexibility and ability to quantify uncertainties make them well-suited for many applications. However, their applicability to large datasets is limited by the cubic computational time complexity. While reduced-rank methods such as Hilbert space approximations reduce this complexity, scaling to very large datasets remains challenging. Quantum algorithms are promising candidates to further accelerate such computations. Quantum principal component analysis has previously been applied to Hilbert space Gaussian process regression to address this scaling limitation. However, its applicability is limited by the requirement for fault-tolerant quantum hardware. In this work, we present a hybrid quantum-classical model for reduced-rank Gaussian process regression, where we apply a quantum principal component analysis algorithm based on parameterized quantum circuits to Hilbert space Gaussian process regression. In noiseless simulations on a one-dimensional test function, the resulting model reaches a regression accuracy comparable to that of the exact Gaussian process and the classical Hilbert space Gaussian process. The framework uses shallow parameterized circuits and does not require fault-tolerant quantum hardware, which makes it a candidate for noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices.

papers.title: A Fatigue Life Prediction Method Based on Optimized Data Augmentation Algorithm and Adaptive Sampling Model
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Machine learning–based fatigue life prediction is essential; yet their datasets typically contain fewer than 50 samples, severely challenging predictive modeling. This study proposes an integrated framework of simulated annealing (SA)‐guided data augmentation and residual‐driven adaptive sampling (RAS) bagging ensemble. SA optimization identifies augmentation parameters that maximize RAS‐bagging performance, while RAS adaptively reweights bootstrap sampling toward high‐residual regions to enhance ensemble diversity. Repeated nested cross‐validation (tenfold, 30 repetitions with identical splits) showed significant improvements over classical bagging on the CFRP () and DH36 () datasets (Wilcoxon signed‐rank test, all ; large effect sizes, Cliff's ). Mean improved from to and from to , respectively, while mean MAE was reduced by 85.8% and 64.3%, and the standard deviation of decreased by more than an order of magnitude (0.57–0.02 and 1.48–0.13). In addition, the 80% conformal prediction intervals derived from the proposed model achieved an empirical coverage rate of 84%, providing conservative lower‐bound life estimates for reliability‐oriented decision‐making. These results demonstrate that physically bounded data augmentation combined with adaptive ensemble resampling effectively alleviates data scarcity in fatigue life prediction within the studied datasets. Validation on larger independent cohorts, field data, and online learning scenarios is warranted before the framework can be extended to automotive reliability assessment and structural health monitoring.

papers.title: AI-driven multi-agent digital twin conceptual framework for real-time domestic water quality monitoring, purification and smart billing
papers.abstract: Access to safe drinking water remains a critical global challenge, with over 2.2 billion people lacking reliable access despite water’s abundance, as only 3% of Earth’s water is freshwater. Current systems suffer from unreliable analog metering, tampering risks, and the absence of real-time platforms for monitoring quality, consumption, purification and billing—creating a literature gap in scalable, integrated, and intelligent water management solutions. To address this situation, a pilot-scale, machine learning–enabled multi-agent digital twin-inspired framework is developed for domestic water systems, integrating IoT sensors to continuously monitor key parameters (pH, turbidity, temperature, flow, and TDS); purification status; and employing predictive models for anomaly detection and forecasting. Among several tested algorithms (ARIMA, autoregression, and additive regression), additive regression demonstrated comparatively better performance under the constraints of the pilot dataset, relatively low error rates were achieved under evaluation conditions for temperature, pH, flow, pressure, TDS and color. The system links to a web-based platform providing real-time visualization, automated billing, and user alerts, while incorporating an integrated purification module capable of reducing heavy metals and microbial load with above 96.96% accuracy. These actions result in a compact end-to-end prototype framework that demonstrates the feasibility of safe real-time water use under controlled conditions while improving accountability, reducing billing errors, and promoting conservation through predictive alerts. The novelty lies in the seamless integration of IoT sensing, ML-driven analytics, purification, and digital billing into a pilot-scale integrated digital twin framework. This system offers future prospects for deployment in smart city infrastructures, enhanced resilience through cybersecurity integration, and alignment with SDG 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation), indicating its potential as a future step toward scalable water management solutions. However, the system is validated under limited pilot-scale deployment conditions, and further large-scale validation is required.

papers.title: Instability-Aware Digital Twins for Robust Co-Optimization of Operational Carbon Emissions, Thermal Comfort, and Structural Serviceability Reliability under Uncertainty in Smart Buildings
papers.abstract: Modern smart buildings operate under continuously varying climatic, occupancy, equipment, grid-carbon, material, degradation, and sensing conditions, making nominal optimization insufficient for reliable operational decision-making. This study develops and numerically evaluates an instability-aware digital twin for robust co-optimization of operational carbon emissions, occupied-zone thermal discomfort, and component-level structural serviceability reliability under uncertainty. The framework combines a multi-rate thermal–energy–moisture–IAQ–structural model, carbon-aware CO₂-based ventilation control, extended Kalman filtering, Monte Carlo uncertainty propagation, FORM and design-point importance sampling, Gaussian-process surrogate modeling, NSGA-II, and dimensionless objective- and decision-instability metrics. A controlled six-zone benchmark represents a six-story office building with a gross floor area of 10,200 m² over a one-year operational horizon and a 20-year reliability horizon. Re-evaluation of the nominally selected P0 policy under the full modeled uncertainty set increased carbon emissions from 42.6 to 50.4 kgCO₂e m⁻² year⁻¹, occupied zone-time discomfort from 115 to 128 K h year⁻¹, and the serviceability limit-state exceedance probability from 0.021 to 0.031. The corresponding nominal-input underestimations were 15.5% for carbon and 32.3% for the exceedance probability. The selected robust policy produced 48.8 kgCO₂e m⁻² year⁻¹, 98 K h year⁻¹, and PSLS = 0.012, with a reliability index of 2.257. Relative to the uncertainty-aware P0 evaluation, it reduced carbon by 3.2%, discomfort by 23.4%, PSLS by 61.3%, and decision instability by 65.7%. The robust policy maintained a mean occupied zone-time CO₂ concentration of 684 ppm, a 99th percentile of 821 ppm, and zero occupied zone-hours above 1,000 ppm. Within the controlled numerical benchmark, the results show that Pareto efficiency alone does not establish operational robustness and that explicit instability quantification materially changes policy selection.

papers.title: Machine learning-based prediction of 90-day tensile strength in geopolymer concrete under varying input-variable scenarios
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of the long-term tensile strength (TS) of geopolymer concrete remains a complex challenge owing to the nonlinear and interactive nature of the governing parameters. This study develops and comparatively evaluates four machine-learning models linear regression (LR), decision tree (DT), random forest (RF) and support-vector regression (SVR) to predict 90-day tensile strength from a suite of physicochemical and mixture-related variables. Eleven systematically designed input scenarios were formulated to quantify the influence of different feature combinations on predictive performance. The results demonstrate a pronounced dependence of model accuracy on input configuration. Early scenarios that employed limited variable sets yielded only moderate performance (R² ≤ 0.885, with most models below 0.86), whereas the optimal configuration (S11), which incorporates water absorption (WA), ground-granulated blast-furnace slag (GGBS), nano-silica, pH and bulk density (BD), substantially enhanced predictive capability. Among the models, DT achieved the highest test accuracy (R² = 0.984, RMSE = 0.751) together with the smallest generalisation gap (training R² = 0.988), indicating strong predictive performance within the investigated dataset and limited evidence of overfitting under the applied validation procedures. RF and SVR also delivered high predictive performance (R² = 0.964 and 0.956, respectively), while LR exhibited comparatively lower accuracy, underscoring the importance of nonlinear modelling approaches. Permutation-importance sensitivity analysis identified WA as the dominant influential parameter (mean ΔR² = 0.911), followed by GGBS (0.588) and nano-silica (0.277), indicating that WA and GGBS were the strongest predictors of TS within the trained model, consistent with though not a direct proof of their established physical roles in porosity and geopolymeric gel formation. Collectively, the findings indicate that the integration of advanced tree-based learning algorithms with comprehensive input characterisation provides a promising and computationally efficient framework for modelling the long-term tensile behaviour of geopolymer concrete within the range of mixtures examined; broader industrial application will, however, require external validation on independent datasets and formal uncertainty quantification.

papers.title: Digital twin forestry as an informatics framework integrating remote sensing ecosystem modelling and data assimilation
papers.abstract: Forests are essential to the Earth system, regulating carbon, water, and biodiversity cycles while underpinning ecosystem resilience. Yet they face mounting pressures from climate and land-use change, requiring integrative informatics approaches that link high-resolution observations with advanced ecosystem models. This systematic review defines Digital Twin Forestry (DTF) as an emerging paradigm that continuously couples multisensor Earth Observation data with ecosystem models through data assimilation, enabling dynamic, uncertainty-aware forecasting and adaptive decision support. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we synthesized 57 peer-reviewed studies published between 2016 and 2025 that combined EO datasets with ecosystem modeling and assimilation frameworks. Demonstrated advances include CubeSat constellations, spaceborne LiDAR, UAV hyperspectral systems, and hybrid machine-learning surrogates. Data assimilation methods such as Ensemble Kalman Filters and Particle Filters serve as computational bridges between multi-temporal observations and dynamic model states. Results reveal uneven biome representation, with tropical and boreal forests underrepresented compared to temperate zones, underscoring equity concerns in biodiversity-rich regions. While most forestry digital twins remain at prototype or early operational stages, continuous coupling of sensing platforms to models demonstrates the potential for near-real-time forecasting that extends beyond static inventories. Future priorities include physics-informed machine learning, FAIR-compliant cloud-native workflows, and expanded monitoring in underrepresented ecosystems. Embedding biodiversity and resilience monitoring into near-real-time, uncertainty-aware workflows will be critical, enabling DTF to evolve into operational systems that provide adaptive, policy-relevant decision support for climate-resilient forest management. This review offers an integrative roadmap for advancing DTF, contributing to global sustainability and supporting the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, including Climate Action (SDG 13) and Life on Land (SDG 15).

papers.title: The Evolution of Biotechnology: Historical Discoveries, Major Milestones, and Recent Advances: A Comprehensive Review
papers.abstract: Biotechnology has evolved from ancient fermentation practices and the domestication of plants and animals into a multidisciplinary field that integrates molecular biology, genetics, engineering, and computational sciences.This review presents a comprehensive overview of the historical evolution of biotechnology, highlighting the major scientific discoveries, technological milestones, and recent advances that have shaped its development.Early contributions by Robert Hooke, Antonie van Leeuwenhoek, Louis Pasteur, Gregor Mendel, and Karl Ereky established the foundations of cell biology, microbiology, genetics, and industrial biotechnology.Subsequent breakthroughs, including the elucidation of the DNA double helix, recombinant DNA technology, recombinant human insulin, the Human Genome Project, and CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing, revolutionized biological research and enabled transformative applications in medicine, agriculture, and industry.The review further discusses advances in genome engineering, viral and non-viral gene delivery systems, synthetic biology, regenerative medicine, tissue engineering, bioprinting, biofortification, cellular agriculture, and sustainable biomanufacturing.Recent innovations involving high-throughput sequencing, multi-omics technologies, messenger RNA therapeutics, artificial intelligence, protein structure prediction, and computational protein design have accelerated biological discovery and expanded the capabilities of precision medicine and biotechnology.The review also examines the emergence of biotechnology regulation, the development of the bioeconomy, and the growing importance of ethical, safe, and sustainable implementation of biotechnology.Collectively, these developments demonstrate the remarkable progression of biotechnology from traditional biological practices to advanced genome engineering and AI-driven innovation, emphasizing its critical role in addressing global challenges in healthcare, agriculture, environmental sustainability, food security, and industrial development.

papers.title: A review of offline training of robotic manipulator control under limited data
papers.abstract: Offline reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as a promising paradigm for robotic skill acquisition, particularly for manipulation tasks where real-world trial-and-error interaction is costly, time-consuming, or unsafe. In contrast to broad offline RL surveys, this paper presents a focused narrative review centered on robotic manipulation under data-limited conditions, where datasets often suffer from narrow state–action coverage, sparse successful demonstrations, noisy trajectories, and limited behavioral diversity. These constraints exacerbate key challenges in offline RL, including distributional shift, unstable value estimation, weak reward propagation under sparsity, and poor policy generalization. This paper adopts a focused narrative review methodology; it does not claim systematic review status and does not follow a PRISMA protocol, but instead provides a structured, evidence-informed synthesis of representative offline RL methods selected for their methodological significance, benchmark relevance, and applicability to data-limited robotic manipulation conditions. The review analyzes major families of offline RL methods, including conservative value-based approaches, behavior-constrained learning, advantage-weighted methods, uncertainty-aware techniques, model-based offline RL, sequence-modeling approaches, and offline-to-online adaptation strategies. The discussion is grounded in benchmark observations from D4RL and NeoRL, alongside evidence from robotic manipulation systems such as QT-Opt and RoboNet. Comparative analysis suggests that conservative and uncertainty-aware methods typically offer stronger robustness and policy stability under constrained robotic datasets, whereas behavior-constrained and advantage-based approaches remain highly sensitive to dataset quality, behavioral diversity, and reward structure. Model-based and sequence-modeling methods can further improve data efficiency and long-horizon capability, but introduce additional challenges related to model reliability, synthetic rollout fidelity, and sequential data requirements. The paper also discusses practical issues in real-world deployment, including safety constraints, contact instability, sensor noise, and safe online adaptation. Finally, it highlights future research directions such as uncertainty-aware learning, physics-informed world models, foundation models, representation learning, and safe offline-to-online adaptation for robotic manipulation. Overall, this review provides a targeted synthesis of offline RL methods for robotic manipulation under realistic data-scarce conditions, while identifying key limitations, benchmark trends, and open research challenges for next-generation robotic learning systems.

papers.title: Clarifying moderate and nearly isotropic lattice thermal transport in metastable δ-Ga2O3
papers.abstract: The intrinsic lattice thermal transport of metastable δ-Ga 2 O 3 remains insufficiently clarified, although thermal transport in other Ga 2 O 3 polymorphs has been widely investigated. Because of its cubic bixbyite-type structure, δ-Ga 2 O 3 has been suggested to possibly possess relatively high and weakly anisotropic lattice thermal conductivity, but its actual conductivity magnitude and phonon-level transport mechanism remain unclear. Here, we construct a dedicated neuroevolution potential for single-phase δ-Ga 2 O 3 through active learning and validate it using density functional theory (DFT) phonon dispersion and first-principles ShengBTE thermal conductivity calculations. Homogeneous nonequilibrium molecular dynamics simulations show that the 300 K lattice thermal conductivities of δ-Ga 2 O 3 along the [100], [010], and [001] directions are 5.85 ± 0.15, 5.90 ± 0.20, and 5.90 ± 0.20 W m −1 K −1 , respectively, indicating nearly isotropic thermal transport within statistical uncertainty. The first-principles ShengBTE calculation gives a room-temperature lattice thermal conductivity of 5.96 W m −1 K −1 , further confirming that the lattice thermal conductivities of Ga 2 O 3 polymorphs follow the order β > α > δ > γ ≥ κ(ε). Compared with other Ga 2 O 3 polymorphs, δ-Ga 2 O 3 exhibits the weakest thermal anisotropy among the phases considered. Phonon-resolved analyses reveal that its nearly isotropic behavior is associated with similar mean free path and spectral thermal conductivity distributions along the three principal directions, whereas its moderate thermal conductivity mainly originates from shortened low-frequency phonon mean free paths. These results clarify the intrinsic thermal transport characteristics of metastable δ-Ga 2 O 3 and establish its position among Ga 2 O 3 polymorphs through comparative analysis with other phases.

papers.title: Resource-efficient machine learning via multi-staged feature elimination for sustainable structural assessment and life-extension of FRP-strengthened RC beams
papers.abstract: Retrofitting existing structures to extend service life is vital for reducing the built environment's massive footprint, which accounts for 40% of global energy use and solid waste. Fiber-Reinforced Polymer (FRP) strengthening is a widely used retrofit technique for reinforced concrete (RC) beams. However, assessing whether a strengthened beam will perform safely traditionally depends on extensive laboratory testing of geometric and material properties, a process that is costly, slow, and resource-intensive. This study evaluates whether reliable structural assessment can be achieved with a reduced parameter set, thereby minimizing the testing burden. Using an experimental database of 624 FRP-strengthened RC beam specimens, we developed machine learning models that jointly predict governing failure mode and ultimate load capacity, achieving Macro-F1 = 0.93 and MCC = 0.91 for classification, and R 2 = 0.96 (RMSE = 9.59 kN) for capacity prediction under a random specimen-level evaluation protocol, with additional grouped and leave-one-study-out cross-validation performed to assess generalization across independent source studies. Beyond predictive accuracy, this study's central contribution is a staged feature-elimination pipeline combining Boruta screening, cross-validated SHAP and permutation importance ranking, and factorial ablation with paired statistical significance testing corrected for the non-independence of repeated cross-validation folds and for multiple comparisons. Results demonstrate that two input variables, including FRP tensile strength, whose determination requires destructive coupon testing, can be eliminated with no statistically significant loss in predictive performance on the holdout test set, a conclusion further supported by robustness checks across alternative model families and by uncertainty quantification via bootstrap confidence intervals. This reduces the required input set from 12 to 10, establishing a validated minimum viable assessment parameter set that meaningfully cuts the testing, time, and resource burden of retrofit decision-making, while also lowering model training time by approximately 15%, in qualitative alignment with SDG 9, SDG 12, and SDG 13.

papers.title: Digital Twin-Based Modeling and Optimization of Continuous Biomanufacturing Processes: A Data-Driven Simulation Study
papers.abstract: Continuous biomanufacturing, particularly perfusion-based monoclonal-antibody production, offers highproductivity and consistent quality but requires faster, more reliable monitoring and control thanconventional fed-batch operation. This paper reviews digital-twin-based optimisation of continuousbiomanufacturing and presents an illustrative, reproducible simulation informed by publicly availablebioprocess datasets. A three-tier digital-model, digital-shadow, and digital-twin architecture is examinedalongside mechanistic, data-driven, and hybrid modelling paradigms. The simulation demonstrates modelpredictive control of glucose set-point tracking in a perfusion bioreactor. Across the reviewed studies andillustrative results, hybrid mechanistic-machine-learning twins provide stronger predictive performancethan purely mechanistic or data-driven alternatives, while digital-twin-based control reduces glucosedeviation relative to conventional control and open-loop feeding. Key barriers include fragmenteddatasets, model validation, regulatory acceptance, cybersecurity, and cross-scale transferability. The studytherefore recommends open, standardised bioprocess datasets and rigorous deployment validation tosupport reproducible, industrially credible digital-twin research.

papers.title: A systematic and critical review of artificial intelligence applications for enhancing well stimulation operations and sustainable reservoir management
papers.abstract: Well stimulation remains essential for improving reservoir productivity, but conventional workflows are constrained by geological heterogeneity, limited data, and dependence on empirical correlations. This systematic and comparative review examines artificial-intelligence applications in hydraulic fracturing, acidizing, sand control, and ultrasonic stimulation, focusing on 2020–2025 while selectively considering earlier foundational studies. The quantitative synthesis of 23 key application studies identified 11 studies on acidizing and acid fracturing (47.8%), 8 on hydraulic fracturing (34.8%), 3 on sand control (13.0%), and 1 on ultrasonic stimulation (4.3%). Neural-network architectures were reported in 16 studies (69.6%), while tree-based learners or ensembles appeared in 13 studies (56.5%); these categories overlap because several studies compared multiple algorithms. Among studies reporting numerical performance, R2 values for acidizing-related regression tasks ranged from 0.82 to 0.96, while reported classification accuracies for selected acidizing and sand-control applications ranged from 87.5% to above 90%. These values were not statistically pooled because the studies used different prediction targets, data scales, validation procedures, and performance definitions. Tree-based ensembles and neural networks currently dominate fracture-design and acidizing applications, whereas reinforcement learning, hybrid optimization, and physics-informed approaches remain less frequently investigated. Field-scale and cross-field validation are limited, particularly for sand control and ultrasonic stimulation, for which the available evidence is predominantly laboratory- or simulation-based. The principal barriers to operational deployment are proprietary and small datasets, inconsistent validation, limited interpretability, and uncertain model transferability. Future research should prioritize benchmark datasets, standardized reporting, external field validation, explainable and physics-constrained models, and carefully evaluated closed-loop stimulation systems. papers.title: Material extrusion-based additive manufacturing of aluminum feedstocks with a focus on the debinding process
papers.abstract: Abstract This study investigates the printability, debinding, and sinterability of aluminum-based (AA6061) feedstocks prepared with three different commercial thermoplastic binder compositions, with focus on the effect of the post-processing on microstructure and densification during sintering. Two debinding approaches were studied: (i) solvent debinding followed by thermal debinding, and (ii) single-step wick debinding, in which the green parts were embedded in a powder bed. Debinding is the most challenging stage for Al-containing feedstocks. The strong tendency of aluminum to oxidize significantly restricts the choice of solvent and limits debinding in an oxygen-containing atmosphere. To avoid oxidation of aluminum powder, the solvent type and debinding temperature in air must be restricted. This limitation can leave residues of carbon in the structure during sintering in a nitrogen atmosphere. Based on simultaneous thermal gravimetric analysis, the onset oxidation temperature for the 6061 aluminum powder used in this study was determined to be approximately 400 °C; therefore, the thermal debinding temperature under air was selected below this limit. The results showed that with both debinding methods, binder removal of ≥ 96% could be achieved. However, optical microscopy and density measurements after sintering indicated that even high-purity acetone as a solvent medium resulted in slight oxidation, particularly at the printed sample surfaces. Interestingly, wick debinding without previous solvent debinding resulted in samples with higher post-sintering density. The effect of sintering dwell time was also examined. Increasing the holding time from 2 h to 10 h improved the relative density from ~ 97% to ~ 98%.

papers.title: Dynamic pricing for improved parking space utilization: a data-driven Bayesian optimization approach
papers.abstract: Parking scarcity in downtown areas presents a major challenge for commuters seeking convenient spaces near their destinations. This study proposes a dynamic pricing optimization framework for garage parking in downtown Chicago, balancing the often-conflicting objectives of garage operators and users. The framework formulates garage pricing as a multi-objective optimization problem that combines normalized garage revenue and occupancy, with the weight factors calibrated through a sensitivity analysis to identify the trade-off that maximizes occupancy gains while approximately preserving baseline garage revenue. Using simulated POLARIS data, we applied a Bayesian optimization framework to determine the optimal garage prices for both peak and off-peak periods, then evaluated key performance metrics, including the temporal and spatial distribution of garage fees, occupancy rates, and revenues over a 24-hour period. Results showed that the optimized pricing strategy substantially reduced off-peak garage fees, improving accessibility during off-peak periods, while peak-period fees remained close to existing baseline levels, avoiding disadvantage to peak-period travelers. Peak-hour occupancy increased from approximately 50% to over 70%, with improved overall parking space utilization and limited revenue trade-off. The study also highlights the influence of allocating a portion of parking spaces to other road users.

papers.title: Enhancing Hypothyroid Severity Classification through Bayesian Optimization of Machine Learning Models
papers.abstract: Objective: A person with undiagnosed or ineffectively assessed hypothyroidism may lead to serious metabolic and cardiovascular problems. Existing diagnostic methods mainly focus on binary classification (hypothyroid vs. non-hypothyroid) and frequently oversee the need to stratify patients by severity level, which is serious for guiding treatment intensity. This study proposes to develop a machine learning outline that not only expects the presence of hypothyroidism but also categorizes its severity level, using Bayesian Optimization to perfect model performance for enhanced diagnostic precision. Methods: A clinical dataset comprising thyroid function indicators such as TSH, T3, T4, FTI, and patient demographic/clinical traits was used to figure a multi-class classification model for hypothyroid severity levels like mild, moderate and severe hypothyroidism. Data preprocessing comprises of handling missing values, imbalanced dataset, and feature selection. Several baseline classifiers including Random Forest, K-Nearest Neighbour and Support Vector Machine were trained, and Bayesian Optimization was employed to methodically search the hyperparameter space of these models, optimizing parameters like maximum depth of the tree, minimum number of leaves, minimum sample split, number of estimators, selection of criterion. Model performance metrics was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score with cross-validation confirming robustness against overfitting. Findings: The Bayesian-optimized models constantly outperformed their grid-search on randomized search cross validation, attaining better classification accuracy and more balanced precision and recall across severity classes. The optimized ensemble model established strong discriminative capability in clinical mild, moderate and severe hypothyroid cases, which are frequently clinically unclear. Feature importance analysis was revealed that TSH and FTI levels were the most significant predictors of severity, positioning with recognized clinical understanding. Novelty: Distinct prior studies that mainly address hypothyroidism as a binary classification problem, this study introduces a severity level prediction, offering fine tunes diagnostic support. The combination of Bayesian Optimization for hyperparameter tuning rather than conservative grid or random search CV, it provided a more efficient and adaptive optimization process, dropping computational cost while improving predictive accuracy. This combination of severity level-based organization and optimized hyperparameter tuning method represents a novel contribution towards building clinically meaningful, precise, and effective hypothyroid diagnostic support systems.

papers.title: Additive manufacturing of biomedical Ti-Ta alloy from pre-alloyed powder: An attempt to balance affordability, manufacturability and functionality
papers.abstract: Additive manufacturing of biomedical Ti-Ta alloys has largely relied on elemental powder feedstocks, which often suffer from incomplete melting of refractory Ta particles and pronounced chemical inhomogenery. In this study, a relatively cost-effective pre-alloyed Ti-60Ta (wt.%) powder feedstock, produced by powder metallurgy (PM) followed by electrode induction melting gas atomisation (EIGA), was used to fabricate Ti-60Ta via laser powder bed fusion. The powder contained approximately 12.5 wt.% incompletely dissolved Ta and the remainder Ti-54.3Ta alloy. Despite incomplete pre-alloying, the resulting builds showed substantially improved compositional and microstructural homogeneity compared with Ti–Ta alloys fabricated from elemental powders. Increasing the energy density from 54.2 J/mm³ to 156.8 J/mm³ promoted further Ta dissolution and β-phase stabilisation, but reduced build density and promoted microstructural coarsening. Both processing conditions produced Ti–60Ta with compressive strength comparable to β phase-dominated Ti-Ta alloys produced by any means, and excellent ductility with no macroscopic fracture up to 35% strain. Cracks propagated preferentially along residual-Ta-derived dendritic/equiaxed grain clusters and grain-boundary secondary phases. In vitro assay showed primary osteoblasts well adhered to and proliferated on either polished or as-built Ti-60Ta surfaces, comparable to their response on benchmark biomaterial Ti-6Al-4V. These findings demonstrate the potential of incompletely pre-alloyed PM-EIGA Ti-Ta powders as a cost-effective feedstock for AM Ti-Ta, shedding light on the balance among feedstock affordability, manufacturability, mechanical performance, and biological functionality for Ti-Ta implant applications.

papers.title: Quantitative structure-property mapping and target-driven design of Voronoi porous tantalum scaffolds fabricated by selective laser melting
papers.abstract: Voronoi porous tantalum (Ta) scaffolds are promising for bone repair, but relationships among design, structure, and mechanics remain insufficiently defined. This study aimed to establish a design framework driven by target mechanical performance for Voronoi porous Ta scaffolds fabricated by selective laser melting (SLM). Point spacing and strut diameter were varied to map porosity and specific surface area. Six groups with designed porosities of 65% to 90% underwent manufacturability assessment, quasistatic compression testing, and finite element analysis (FEA). SLM reproduced interconnected Voronoi networks, with strut diameter deviations of 21 to 29.2 μm and porosity deviations of 1.90% to 2.75%. Nonlinear mappings from point spacing and strut diameter to porosity and specific surface area yielded R 2 values of 0.997 and 0.998, respectively. As porosity increased from 65% to 90%, elastic modulus decreased from 1892 ± 77 to 231 ± 30 MPa and yield strength from 30.60 ± 1.69 to 3.77 ± 0.27 MPa, with R 2 values of 0.998 and 0.962 for power law fits. FEA of parameter combinations with similar porosity showed comparable mechanical properties, indicating that, within the investigated range, porosity is a key intermediate variable linking design parameters to mechanics. Although FEA overpredicted absolute values, it captured trends associated with porosity and revealed a topology dependent progressive load transfer process involving selective local load bearing, progressive strut recruitment, and continuous stress redistribution. These relationships enable an inverse design pathway from target mechanical properties to porosity and design parameters, supporting predictable design of Voronoi porous Ta scaffolds fabricated by SLM.

papers.title: EFEKTIVITAS PENERAPAN MODEL PROBLEM-BASED LEARNING (PBL) BERBASIS DEEP LEARNING TERHADAP KEAKTIFAN SISWA IPS KELAS VIIIE
papers.abstract: This study aims to examine the effectiveness of implementing a Problem-Based Learning (PBL) model integrated with Deep Learning to improve student engagement in Social Studies (IPS) in Class VIIE at Brawijaya Smart School (BSS), Malang. The study was motivated by low student engagement, reflected in limited participation in discussions, reluctance to express opinions, and minimal involvement in question-and-answer activities. These issues indicate the need for more innovative learning approaches to overcome teacher-centered instruction. The integration of PBL and Deep Learning was selected to encourage contextual problem-solving, critical thinking, collaboration, and deeper conceptual understanding. This quantitative study employed a one-group pretest-posttest design involving 31 students from Class VIIE at SMP BSS Malang. Data were collected using a student engagement questionnaire and an observation sheet. The questionnaire employed a five-point Likert scale and was subjected to validity and reliability testing. Data analysis involved the Kolmogorov-Smirnov normality test and a paired-samples t-test. The normality test yielded significance values of 0.296 for the pretest and 0.072 for the posttest, indicating that both datasets met the normality assumption at the 5% significance level. The paired-samples t-test revealed a statistically significant difference in student engagement before and after the intervention (t = 28.030; p < 0.001). These findings indicate increased student engagement following the implementation of Deep Learning-based PBL. Therefore, this integrated model may serve as an alternative approach to Social Studies instruction that promotes student participation, collaboration, critical thinking, and problem-solving. Keywords: Problem-Based Learning, Deep Learning, student engagement, Social Studies, active learning. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis efektivitas penerapan model Problem-Based Learning (PBL) berbasis Deep Learning dalam meningkatkan keaktifan siswa pada mata pelajaran Ilmu Pengetahuan Sosial (IPS) kelas VIIE SMP Brawijaya Smart School (BSS) Malang. Penelitian ini dilatarbelakangi oleh rendahnya keaktifan siswa yang terlihat dari terbatasnya partisipasi dalam diskusi, kurangnya keberanian mengemukakan pendapat, dan minimnya keterlibatan dalam kegiatan tanya jawab. Kondisi tersebut menunjukkan perlunya pendekatan pembelajaran inovatif untuk mengatasi pembelajaran yang masih berpusat pada guru. Integrasi PBL dan Deep Learning dipilih untuk mendorong pemecahan masalah kontekstual, berpikir kritis, kolaborasi, dan pemahaman konsep secara mendalam. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan desain one-group pretest-posttest yang melibatkan 31 siswa kelas VIIE SMP BSS Malang. Data dikumpulkan melalui angket keaktifan siswa dan lembar observasi. Angket menggunakan skala Likert lima tingkat serta telah melalui pengujian validitas dan reliabilitas. Analisis data dilakukan menggunakan uji normalitas Kolmogorov-Smirnov dan paired-samples t-test. Hasil uji normalitas menunjukkan nilai signifikansi sebesar 0,296 pada pretest dan 0,072 pada posttest, sehingga keduanya memenuhi asumsi normalitas pada taraf signifikansi 5%. Hasil paired-samples t-test menunjukkan perbedaan keaktifan siswa yang signifikan sebelum dan sesudah perlakuan (t = 28,030; p < 0,001). Temuan ini menunjukkan peningkatan keaktifan siswa setelah penerapan PBL berbasis Deep Learning. Dengan demikian, model terintegrasi ini berpotensi menjadi alternatif pembelajaran IPS yang mendorong partisipasi, kolaborasi, berpikir kritis, dan pemecahan masalah. papers.abstract: This article presents a qualitative review of international and Kazakhstani research on teaching biology with augmented reality (AR) and virtual reality (VR) technologies in secondary schools and higher education institutions. The review draws on meta-analyses, systematic reviews and empirical studies published between 2014 and 2025. The analysis shows that AR has a moderate to large positive effect on biology learning outcomes (e.g., d = 1.13 for school students), whereas the effect of VR is small to moderate (g ≈ 0.24–0.33). At the same time, effectiveness was found to depend less on the technology itself than on the instructional approach used to integrate it into the lesson: active learning tasks, management of cognitive load and the guiding role of the teacher. The article proposes a methodological model of an AR/VR-based biology lesson and discusses the challenges of implementation in Kazakhstani schools and directions for future research.

papers.title: Spectral Limits of Polynomial Graph Filters on the Long-Range Ising Model Benchmark
papers.abstract: The Long-Range Ising Model benchmark (LRIM) guarantees long-range dependence by construction: each label is the node's spin times the spin field convolved with a power-law coupling, so any model's distance from the target is measurable. We prove that a readout whose filter is a polynomial in the adjacency, the linear core of isotropic message passing and spectral graph networks, leaves an error floor that no degree lowers, because the target varies along a level set of the spectrum on which every such filter is constant. Computed exactly, the floor and the best filter of each degree predict two spectral networks adapted from published architectures to within a tenth of a decade. A filter escapes the floor only if it weighs separately the offsets the adjacency lumps together, and must still resolve the coupling across the whole lattice. A strided filter of about fifty coefficients does both: fitted to the training labels, its test error is 52 times below the best published network's. A dilated convolutional network beats the best published result at 256 nodes, matches it at 1,024, and gives the first in-domain results at the three larger sizes, while a Fourier neural operator with its standard modes falls further behind as the lattice grows. At its standard budget the dilated network stays two to four orders of magnitude short of a larger strided filter fitted to the labels. The analysis carries over to the benchmark's second coupling.

papers.title: GlobeBench: Evaluating Text-Based World Model Capabilities for Scalable Environment Simulations
papers.abstract: Text-based world models have recently shown potential to simulate complex RL environment state transitions for a diverse set of use cases. However, no standardized benchmark exists to compare, study and improve these models. Through this paper, we attempt to solve this problem by building GlobeBench, a novel benchmark with 1,632 tasks across five separate domains and nineteen simulation skills. The tasks check whether models can predict the environment's response to a specific action given the full agent trajectory by understanding earlier state changes, following environment rules, and predicting the effects of actions on both related and unrelated objects. We compare the predicted environment response with an execution-derived reference, using a hybrid architecture with both deterministic gates and a semantic judge. Among 20 general-purpose LLMs and specialized text world models, GPT-6 Astra achieves the highest task success rate at 49.57%. We find that model accuracy decreases as actions affect a larger portion of the environment. Specifically, when the agent's changes must propagate to dependent objects, task success drops to an average of 5.1% across all 20 models. Although model strengths differ across tasks, 631 tasks remain unsolved by any model, suggesting a significant gap in general LLM capabilities as a world model.

papers.title: Is a Linear Probe Evidence of a Linear Representation?
papers.abstract: The linear representation hypothesis holds that pretrained vision models encode generative factors as linearly decodable directions in feature space, and comes with a standard methodology: train a linear probe, declare a factor represented if accuracy is high. We show this test is too permissive. Asymptotically, any sufficiently rich feature map, including a random one, admits a linear readout, so high probe accuracy is consistent with two very different geometries: a true linear world model, where the latent-aligned subspace dominates the representation, or a kernel machine, where the latents lie linearly inside a much larger curved manifold. This distinction matters because the curved structure orthogonal to the probe is relevant for out-of-distribution generalization, robustness, and compositional transfer. We propose three asymmetric diagnostics that distinguish the two cases: reverse predictivity, spectral concentration, and out-of-distribution generalization. We validate them in a fully observed simulation where ground truth is known. Applied to six pretrained vision transformers on SVG-World, our deterministic generative benchmark with paired visual styles, and to two of them on CelebA, they show pretraining produces structure beyond a random kernel but well short of a linear world model. On dSprites, 3D Shapes and MPI3D, forward decodability and latent-aligned variance dissociate. Thus, forward decoding alone does not show that the probed factors align with the dominant geometry of the representation. In summary, our work cautions about the success of linear probes as opposed to truly linear and low dimensional representations.

papers.title: Measuring Mechanistic Uncertainty in Large Language Models via Causal Robustness
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in critical domains, where their susceptibility to hallucinations makes reliable and interpretable uncertainty quantification essential. We introduce the concept of mechanistic uncertainty, which characterizes uncertainty through the stability of the internal mechanisms supporting a model's response. We propose the causal robustness margin, defined as the minimum internal intervention required to deviate the model's output, and operationalize it using Jacobian Lens (Jlens) concept steering vectors. Across three open-source models and five question-answering datasets, we show incorrect and uncertain responses exhibit smaller margins, indicating greater sensitivity to internal interventions, and the causal robustness margin complements conventional output-based uncertainty methods. Finally, in a controlled knowledge injection experiment, correctly learned facts show increased margins after training, suggesting that causal robustness provides a mechanistically grounded signal of uncertainty.

papers.title: Structure-Aware Spatial Kernels for Gaussian Process Distributed Port-Hamiltonian Systems
papers.abstract: Gaussian process distributed port-Hamiltonian systems (GP-dPHS) enable data-driven modeling of distributed dynamical systems while preserving their physical structure. However, standard stationary kernels can be inefficient for spatially heterogeneous systems because they neither exploit known input invariances nor reflect structured spatial dependencies. We address this limitation with a structure-aware kernel design that removes irrelevant state coordinates and decouples state and spatial dependencies through a tensor-product covariance. This modular construction allows qualitative knowledge of spatial heterogeneity to be incorporated by selecting an appropriate spatial kernel without requiring an analytical description of the underlying profile. Numerical experiments on a nonlinear string with periodic, smoothly varying, and semi-piecewise stiffness profiles demonstrate that structural decoupling consistently improves reconstruction accuracy, while profile-matched spatial kernels yield substantially larger gains in force-field and trajectory reconstruction.

papers.title: Learnable Splines for Unstructured Neural Operators
papers.abstract: Neural operators approximate solution operators of partial differential equations at a fraction of the cost of numerical solvers. Efficient grid-based architectures such as the Fourier neural operator (FNO) assume uniform rectangular grids, whereas engineering simulations use large, irregular, and locally refined meshes. We introduce L-SplineFNO, a memory-efficient neural operator that couples an FNO backbone with a sparse, learnable tensor-product B-spline transfer between unstructured meshes and a latent Cartesian grid. A local normalised scatter avoids the geometry-dependent solve of analytic spline transformation while preserving compact support, partition of unity, and spline smoothness by construction. The neural operator, conditioned on global design and operating parameters, learns the mapping of geometry to the field solution. Across six three-dimensional engineering benchmarks, L-SplineFNO achieves strong predictive accuracy while requiring substantially less memory and compute than baseline operators, scaling to 26.6 million nodes in training and 46 million in inference on a single A100 GPU. It also supports zero-shot super-resolution and efficient closed-form spatial derivatives. Uniquely, the analytic spline decoder yields rigorous prediction bounds over continuous space and uncertain parameters, via Bernstein convex hulls and Taylor models, demonstrated on a 29.2-million-node MAST-U tokamak model.

papers.title: An Adaptive-Horizon Graph Neural Operator for coupled surrogate morphodynamic modelling
papers.abstract: Morphodynamic simulations require repeated coupling between hydrodynamic solvers, sediment transport modules, and bed updating. For long duration, multi-scenario simulations on large unstructured meshes, such coupling is computationally demanding. This study proposes an Adaptive-Horizon Graph Neural Operator (AH-GNO) that formulates bed evolution as a graph operator learning problem from recent hydrodynamic and topographic states to predict future bed elevation increments. The model operates directly on the native unstructured meshes. The approach integrates area-weighted graph learning, historical state selection, and forecast horizon estimation, allowing the effective history length (K) and update interval (B) to vary with the evolving flow and bed state. Using Telemac2D/GAIA solutions as supervised numerical references, the framework is evaluated on the official Bump and Yen bend benchmarks and on a field-scale application (Waiho River, New Zealand). Results show that the AH-GNO reproduces the main patterns of bedform migration, bend-scale erosion and deposition, and localized bed adjustment. Across the three cases, the tested CPU-GPU deployment reduced post-training bed-update workflow time from 12~1204 s with GAIA to 0.08~3.34 s with AH-GNO. This improvement corresponds to deployment-specific accelerations of approximately 150~360 times relative to 4-core GAIA CPU configurations, and with 105~186 times gains for 20-core CPU configurations. These results suggest that, while retaining hydrodynamic feedback from TELEMAC-2D, a learned operator for bed updating can provide an efficient acceleration component for morphodynamic scenario analysis and rapid coupled simulation.

papers.title: Emerging AI for resilient smart-grid fault detection: an evidence-based capability synthesis, maturity assessment, and research roadmap
papers.abstract: Abstract This evidence-based critical review examines how emerging artificial-intelligence (AI) capabilities can strengthen resilient smart-grid fault intelligence. Rather than comparing algorithms primarily by reported accuracy, the review organizes recent fault-detection evidence around operational capabilities: spatial/topology awareness, temporal context, label efficiency, physical consistency, trust and uncertainty, privacy-preserving collaboration, and deployment feasibility. A structured primary-study evidence matrix was developed to extract task, system or dataset, topology, temporal context, robustness, trust, privacy, physics, deployment evidence, and principal limitations. The extracted evidence shows a clear asymmetry in the maturity of emerging approaches. Recent Transformer work demonstrates real-time temporal fault detection on test-system waveforms, self-supervised methods reduce dependence on manually labeled events, physics-informed approaches can narrow the simulation-to-field gap, and graph-based models increasingly address topology and cross-topology generalization. However, external validation, uncertainty quantification, reproducibility, and standardized deployment evidence remain uneven. Based on this evidence, the paper introduces a fault-intelligence evidence maturity profile that avoids reducing readiness to a single generic score. The synthesis leads to an evidence-derived roadmap progressing from trustworthy and data-efficient intelligence to topology- and physics-aware learning, distributed cyber-physical intelligence, and finally integrated safety-bounded decision support. The review deliberately distinguishes demonstrated evidence from plausible future capability and therefore avoids unsupported claims of algorithmic superiority.

papers.title: Bionic nanocoating-mediated near-infrared persistent luminescence photodynamic system for the treatment of periprosthetic joint infection.
papers.abstract: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) is a catastrophic complication of arthroplasty, notoriously difficult to treat due to bacterial biofilms and escalating antibiotic resistance. To address this, we designed a smart, biomimetic photodynamic coating (PL-PS@Ti) for titanium implants, utilizing near-infrared persistent luminescence nanoparticles (NLPLNPs) to achieve deep-tissue, on-demand antibacterial and osteogenic efficacy. We synthesized chromium/europium-doped zinc gallate NLPLNPs coated with dendritic mesoporous silica and conjugated with a silicon phthalocyanine photosensitizer (ZGO NP@DMSN-Si-Pc, or PL-PS). A copper-coordinated polyphenol network anchored these nanocomposites to titanium substrates. We evaluated the acid-responsive singlet oxygen (1O₂) generation and 808 nm-reactivable afterglow of the coating, followed by validation in cell cultures and a rat PJI model. The acidic PJI microenvironment triggered robust 1O₂ generation, which was sustained by periodic 808 nm excitation. In vitro, the coating was highly biocompatible and achieved a 99.5% bactericidal rate. In the rat PJI model, 808 nm activation effectively cleared periprosthetic bacteria and resolved local inflammation. The coating also promoted osseointegration, yielding a bone volume fraction (BV/TV) of 20.66% at the implant interface four weeks post-treatment. The PL-PS@Ti nanocoating provides a microenvironment-responsive, antibiotic-free strategy to manage implant infections. By utilizing reactivable persistent luminescence, it bypasses the thermal damage risks of continuous irradiation. This dual capacity for broad-spectrum bactericidal activity and bone regeneration offers a practical and translatable intervention for arthroplasty-associated infections.

papers.title: Regeneración ósea guiada en defecto óseo horizontal previo a la colocación de implante: reporte de caso
papers.abstract: Horizontal alveolar ridge loss is a common limitation for placing dental implants in an adequate three-dimensional position. Guided bone regeneration is a predictable technique that restores bone volume by means of biomaterials and barrier membranes. The objective was to describe the clinical management of a horizontal bone defect prior to implant placement. A 56-year-old systemically healthy, non-smoking male patient presented with a missing upper right second premolar and a bone width of approximately 3 mm on cone-beam computed tomography. Decortication, particulate xenograft and a slow-resorbing collagen membrane fixed to the periosteum were performed, with tension-free primary closure. Healing was uneventful, without membrane exposure or infection, and the horizontal gain allowed placement of a standard-diameter implant with good primary stability. Guided bone regeneration was an effective and safe alternative for horizontal ridge augmentation.

papers.abstract: Dental implant rehabilitation in the posterior region is a predictable alternative for replacing missing teeth. The objective was to describe the clinical management of a single implant in the posterior region and to contrast it with the evidence on survival, complications and prosthodontic considerations. A 60-year-old female patient without uncontrolled systemic diseases presented with absence of the upper left second premolar due to extensive caries and root fracture. After clinical examination, periapical radiography and cone beam computed tomography, which showed adequate bone height and moderate horizontal resorption, a 4.1 × 10 mm implant was placed in a prosthetically guided position, with adequate primary stability and conventional loading. It was restored with a screw-retained zirconia crown, with satisfactory osseointegration, functional stability and aesthetics. The posterior single implant is a safe option when supported by three-dimensional planning, a maintainable prosthetic design and periodic peri-implant follow-up.

papers.title: Relevancia del conocimiento craneofacial en la formación del estudiante de Odontología
papers.abstract: Dental and craniofacial anatomy holds a central place in the training of dentists from the first semester. The objective was to analyze the relevance of this knowledge for the clinical performance of dentistry students and the strategies that favor its learning. A narrative literature review was conducted in PubMed, SciELO and Google Scholar, and 13 documents were analyzed. The evidence indicates that mastery of anatomy underpins oral surgery, implantology and image interpretation, but that knowledge of structures without clinical application is lost over the years, whereas clinically relevant landmarks are better retained. Virtual reality, simulators, 3D-printed models, gamification and active learning improve spatial understanding and performance. It is concluded that anatomy should be taught in an integrated way with clinical practice and reinforced throughout the degree program.

papers.title: Técnicas de impresión 3D aplicadas a la odontología
papers.abstract: 3D printing has become established in dentistry because of its accuracy and customization. The objective was to describe the main 3D printing techniques used in dentistry and the critical stages of their workflow. A narrative literature review was conducted in PubMed, SciELO, Redalyc and Google Scholar; 17 documents were analyzed. Stereolithography and digital light processing were the preferred techniques for highly detailed parts; laser powder bed fusion, for strong metal frameworks; fused deposition modeling, for low-cost models; and LCD and PolyJet technologies offered high resolution and versatility. The choice depends on the clinical purpose and the material. Post-processing (washing, post-curing and finishing) determined the mechanical properties and biocompatibility. It is concluded that 3D printing is a strategic tool that requires standardized protocols and continuous training.

papers.title: Uso del ABP como metodología activa y participación de la asignatura de Educación Física en diversos proyectos
papers.abstract: Background: Project-Based Learning (PBL) is an active learning methodology that promotes the integration of knowledge, skills, and experiences through contextualized learning situations. Its implementation in rural schools is particularly relevant because it enables curricular content to be connected with students' surroundings, everyday experiences, and sociocultural characteristics. Within this framework, Physical Education can contribute to interdisciplinary development through activities related to movement, recreation, healthy habits, and environmental exploration. Objective: To describe the integration and participation of Physical Education in 16 interdisciplinary projects developed across first to fourth grades of primary education in a rural school. Methodology: A mixed-methods case study was conducted in a rural school through documentary analysis of 16 interdisciplinary projects implemented during one academic year. The participation of Physical Education, the topics addressed, and the activities developed in coordination with other curricular areas were examined. The projects were primarily related to the natural environment, habits, culture, and movement. Results: Physical Education participated in all 16 projects analyzed, demonstrating transversal integration across different learning experiences. Among the specific subject contents, sports were the most frequently addressed topic, whereas body expression and spatial orientation had a lower presence. The participation of Physical Education enabled the incorporation of theoretical and practical activities related to movement, environmental exploration, healthy habits, and various interdisciplinary learning experiences. Conclusions: In the case analyzed, PBL enabled Physical Education to be integrated with theoretical and practical activities and cross-cutting themes, promoting its incorporation into contextualized learning experiences. However, the evidence corresponds to a single school context, and therefore the findings cannot be generalized. Further research involving larger samples and comparative designs is needed to establish more robust evidence regarding the benefits of PBL and the potential for integrating Physical Education in rural contexts.

papers.title: [Transcutaneous osseointegration for amputees: foundational principles and current concepts].
papers.abstract: Transcutaneous osseointegrated prostheses, which anchor titanium alloy implants into the residual limb bone, offer an alternative for amputees suffering from socket-related complications (occurring in up to 75% of cases). The principle is based on the direct titanium-bone interface, which forms a microscopic gap of approximately 20-50 nm that physically blocks bacteria (typically about 500 nm in diameter); combined with the use of high-purity titanium, this makes percutaneous infection risk much lower than that of traditional implants. Mainstream systems include the hollow-screw design (OPRA), the retrograde-nail design (TiTON), and the compression design (Compress), among which TiTON has wide applicability and is mostly implantable in a single-stage surgery. Clinical studies confirm that the technique significantly improves walking efficiency (by about 20%), wearing time, and quality of life, while osseoperception enhances balance and prosthesis embodiment; combined with nerve reconstruction, it can alleviate neuropathic pain. Major complications such as infection (mostly mechanical skin irritation), periprosthetic fractures (mostly traumatic), and implant fracture are rare, and the risk of severe disability or death is only 0.4%, far lower than infection-related risks in joint replacement. Future research should focus on stabilizing the skin penetration site and further exploring the anti-infective mechanisms of the titanium-bone interface to broaden its application.
